Our analysis reveals three key findings: (1) tasks governed by static perception are generally easier than tasks that require transformational event sequences; (2) most models struggle to resolve cross-agent correspondences, with errors increasing with scene complexity; and (3) models show limited ability to leverage geometric cues present in the scene. As an initial step toward addressing these challenges, we explore geometry-guided synthetic view augmentation that generates intermediate transition frames between agent observations, providing auxiliary spatial context that improves performance in certain categories. Overall, our results highlight that multi-agent collaborative reasoning remains an open challenge and an important direction for multimodal embodied systems. The code is available on the project page: this https URL.

AI.tldr: MaRiO is a benchmark for multi-agent collaborative reasoning in MLLMs, where agents observe a shared environment from independent viewpoints, and 23 state-of-the-art MLLMs are evaluated on it. Models struggle most with cross-agent correspondence and geometric cues, and geometry-guided synthetic view augmentation gives only partial gains.
AI.motivation: MLLM evaluations focus on single-view or multi-view settings with shared camera parameters, leaving multi-agent collaboration with independent viewpoints underexplored.
AI.method: The authors introduce the MaRiO benchmark and evaluate 23 MLLMs on it. As an initial step they explore geometry-guided synthetic view augmentation that generates intermediate transition frames between agent observations.
AI.result: Static perception tasks are generally easier than tasks requiring transformational event sequences. Most models struggle to resolve cross-agent correspondences, with errors rising as scene complexity increases, and models make limited use of geometric cues. The augmentation improves performance in certain categories.
AI.conclusion: Multi-agent collaborative reasoning remains an open challenge for multimodal embodied systems, and the work points to a direction for future research.

title: PoseBench: Probing Pose Awareness in Visual Foundation Models
summary: Pose awareness characterizes the extent to which a learned feature space aligns with the underlying object-pose manifold, such that observations with similar poses exhibit greater feature similarity than those with increasingly different poses. While such structure is desirable for pose-sensitive 3D vision tasks, visual foundation models pre-trained on individual 2D images typically lack explicit 3D or pose supervision. This raises a fundamental question: Do 2D visual foundation models exhibit pose awareness after large-scale pretraining? To answer this question, we introduce PoseBench, a systematic benchmark to probe pose awareness in pretrained visual features. Our evaluation follows a progressive design: held-out rendered views probe intrinsic pose-aware structure under controlled conditions, while real-image queries evaluate how robustly this structure remains accessible under real-world variations. We further introduce pose-graph-based refinement as a complementary probe of compatibility between feature neighborhoods and the underlying pose manifold. Across 31 publicly available checkpoints from 10 pretraining families, PoseBench reveals that pose awareness is an implicit but non-uniform property of 2D visual foundation models, and consistent gains from pose-graph refinement suggest that feature spaces retain structure compatible with the underlying pose manifold. PoseBench therefore provides a systematic basis for understanding and selecting pretrained features for pose-sensitive 3D vision tasks.

AI.tldr: PoseBench is a benchmark that probes whether pretrained 2D visual foundation models encode object pose awareness, using rendered held-out views and real-image queries. Across 31 checkpoints from 10 pretraining families, pose awareness is found to be implicit but non-uniform, and pose-graph refinement consistently helps.
AI.motivation: Pose-sensitive 3D vision needs features whose similarity reflects object pose, but 2D foundation models are pretrained without explicit 3D or pose supervision, so it is unclear whether they show pose awareness.
AI.method: A progressive evaluation first uses held-out rendered views to test intrinsic pose-aware structure under controlled conditions, then uses real-image queries to test how robustly that structure is accessible. Pose-graph-based refinement serves as a complementary probe of how well feature neighbourhoods match the pose manifold.
AI.result: Across 31 publicly available checkpoints from 10 pretraining families, pose awareness is an implicit but non-uniform property, and consistent gains from pose-graph refinement suggest that feature spaces retain structure compatible with the pose manifold.
AI.conclusion: PoseBench gives a systematic basis for understanding and selecting pretrained features for pose-sensitive 3D vision tasks.

title: Guided Co-Attention with Adaptive Gating for Multimodal Medical Data Fusion
summary: Multimodal fusion requires not only exchanging information across modalities but also determining which representations should participate in the interaction and how complementary cross-modal views should be combined. We introduce Guided Co-Attention with Adaptive Gating, a fusion framework that integrates token-wise guidance, bidirectional cross-attention, and sample-specific fusion. The proposed method constructs two directional representations: an image-conditioned text representation, obtained by allowing textual tokens to query visual features, and a text-conditioned image representation formed in the reverse direction. Token-wise guidance modulates the representations before cross-attention, while an adaptive gate learns the relative contribution of the two resulting directional representations for each sample. We evaluate the approach using paired chest radiographs and radiology reports as an image-text test bed for binary (normal vs. abnormal) classification. The two cross-attention directions exhibit distinct performance characteristics, demonstrating that reversing the query and source modalities does not produce interchangeable representations. Ablation experiments further show that bidirectional interaction, adaptive gating, and token guidance provide complementary benefits. The proposed model achieves 96.05% accuracy, 96.10% F1-score, 98.37% AUC, 95.60% Sens@95Spec, and 96.51% Spec@95Sens, yielding the highest mean performance across all evaluated metrics. These findings support explicitly modeling interaction direction, token relevance, and sample-dependent integration when constructing multimodal representations.

AI.tldr: The paper proposes Guided Co-Attention with Adaptive Gating for fusing chest radiographs and radiology reports, combining token-wise guidance, bidirectional cross-attention and a per-sample gate. It reaches 96.05% accuracy and 98.37% AUC for normal versus abnormal classification, the highest mean performance across all evaluated metrics.
AI.motivation: Multimodal fusion must decide which representations take part in cross-modal interaction and how complementary views should be combined, and existing approaches do not explicitly model interaction direction.
AI.method: Two directional representations are built: an image-conditioned text representation in which text tokens query visual features, and a text-conditioned image representation in the reverse direction. Token-wise guidance modulates representations before cross-attention, and an adaptive gate learns each direction's contribution per sample.
AI.result: The model achieves 96.05% accuracy, 96.10% F1, 98.37% AUC, 95.60% Sens@95Spec and 96.51% Spec@95Sens, giving the highest mean performance across all evaluated metrics. The two cross-attention directions behave differently, and ablations show that bidirectional interaction, adaptive gating and token guidance each add complementary benefit.
AI.conclusion: Explicitly modelling interaction direction, token relevance and sample-dependent integration is beneficial when constructing multimodal representations.

title: DAPointRWKV: Domain Adaptive Vision RWKV for Point Cloud Completion
comment: This paper has been accepted by 34th ACM International Conference on Multimedia
summary: Domain adaptive point cloud completion (DA PCC) aims to bridge the geometric discrepancy between labeled source domains and unlabeled target domains for accurate 3D shape completion. Existing methods based on CNNs, Transformers, and Mamba-like sequence models still face challenges from limited receptive fields, high computational complexity, insufficient geometric bias, and serialization sensitivity. Recently, Receptance Weighted Key Value (RWKV) provides a linear-complexity alternative for long-range sequence modeling. However, adapting RWKV to DA PCC remains challenging due to the lack of explicit geometric priors, the mismatch between recurrent modeling and coarse-to-fine generation, and unstable target-domain adaptation. To address these challenges, we propose DAPointRWKV, a novel RWKV-based framework for DA PCC. DAPointRWKV consists of three components: Geometry-Aware RWKV (GA-RWKV) Backbone, RWKV-Oriented Progressive Decoder (RWKV-PD), and Dual Structural Regularization (DSR). Specifically, GA-RWKV introduces geometry-aware recurrent representation learning, RWKV-PD bridges RWKV token representations with coarse-to-fine reconstruction through local token-guided refinement, and DSR stabilizes target-domain transfer through visible-structure anchoring and complete-shape hypothesis stabilization. Extensive experiments on synthetic and real-world benchmarks demonstrate that DAPointRWKV consistently outperforms state-of-the-art methods.

AI.tldr: DAPointRWKV is an RWKV-based framework for domain adaptive point cloud completion that combines a geometry-aware backbone, a progressive decoder and dual structural regularisation. It reportedly outperforms state-of-the-art methods on synthetic and real-world benchmarks.
AI.motivation: Domain adaptive point cloud completion needs to bridge geometric discrepancies between labelled source and unlabelled target domains, and CNNs, Transformers and Mamba-like models face limited receptive fields, high cost, weak geometric bias and serialisation sensitivity.
AI.method: Three components are proposed: a Geometry-Aware RWKV backbone that adds geometry-aware recurrent representation learning, an RWKV-Oriented Progressive Decoder that links RWKV tokens to coarse-to-fine reconstruction through local token-guided refinement, and Dual Structural Regularisation that uses visible-structure anchoring and complete-shape hypothesis stabilisation.
AI.result: Extensive experiments on synthetic and real-world benchmarks show that DAPointRWKV consistently outperforms state-of-the-art methods. The abstract gives no numerical results.
AI.conclusion: RWKV, with explicit geometric priors and structural regularisation, is a viable linear-complexity basis for domain adaptive point cloud completion.

title: ClearForm: Shared-Surface Gaussian Splatting for Transparent and Opaque Scenes
summary: Transparent-interface reconstruction must recover glass surfaces even when most observed color comes from the scene behind them. We present ClearForm, a shared-planar-Gaussian method for jointly reconstructing transparent interfaces and the appearance seen through them. We identify and analyze the Geometry-Appearance Compositing Dilemma (GACD): when the same transparency-dependent alpha controls both color and geometry, revealing the background can weaken a transparent surface's contribution to geometric reconstruction. We derive its effect on plane-based depth estimation, identify a mechanism that can weaken geometric learning, and quantify the loss of interface support through controlled comparisons. To address this conflict, we develop geometry-preserving dual-opacity surface reconstruction. Shared planar Gaussians retain interface contributions in geometry compositing while modeling transmission and sparse reflection in RGB, supported by transparency-aware geometric constraints. To manage the different primitive-visibility requirements of these compositors, we introduce Dual-Evidence Lifecycle (DEL), which retains Gaussians supported by multi-view geometry or RGB reconstruction evidence. On 3D-FRONT-T, ClearForm achieves 27.05 mm Chamfer distance (CD) and 0.928 F1, compared with 59.18 mm CD for our PGSR reproduction and the reported 34 mm CD and 0.836 F1 for GLINT. On TransLab, it achieves 1.65 mm CD, 0.963 F1, and 40.14 dB PSNR. In matched ablations, dual-opacity compositing reduces CD from 59.25 to 27.09 mm, while DEL improves PSNR by 2.06 dB. Our project page is available at this https URL.

AI.tldr: ClearForm jointly reconstructs transparent glass interfaces and the scene seen through them using shared planar Gaussians with dual-opacity compositing, which separates geometry compositing from RGB compositing. It achieves 27.05 mm Chamfer distance and 0.928 F1 on 3D-FRONT-T, and 1.65 mm Chamfer distance on TransLab.
AI.motivation: Transparent-interface reconstruction must recover glass surfaces even when most observed colour comes from the background, and using one transparency-dependent alpha for both colour and geometry weakens geometric learning, a conflict the authors name the Geometry-Appearance Compositing Dilemma.
AI.method: Geometry-preserving dual-opacity surface reconstruction keeps interface contributions in geometry compositing while modelling transmission and sparse reflection in RGB, supported by transparency-aware geometric constraints. The Dual-Evidence Lifecycle retains Gaussians supported by either multi-view geometry or RGB reconstruction evidence.
AI.result: On 3D-FRONT-T, ClearForm reaches 27.05 mm Chamfer distance and 0.928 F1, against 59.18 mm for the authors' PGSR reproduction and reported values of 34 mm and 0.836 for GLINT. On TransLab it reaches 1.65 mm Chamfer distance, 0.963 F1 and 40.14 dB PSNR. Dual-opacity compositing lowers Chamfer distance from 59.25 to 27.09 mm, and DEL improves PSNR by 2.06 dB.
AI.conclusion: Separating geometry and appearance opacity resolves the compositing dilemma and enables accurate reconstruction of transparent interfaces together with the background.

title: PhysDNet: Physics-Driven Gradient Amplification for Real-Time Image Dehazing
comment: Accepted to NeurIPS 2026. Code, deployment scripts and pre-trained checkpoints: this https URL
summary: Modern dehazing networks are often computationally expensive and overfit to synthetic haze, limiting real-time deployment. This underscores an urgent demand for efficient, high-fidelity restoration methods that can operate on resource-constrained edge devices in practical, dynamic environments. We introduce PhysDNet, a lightweight multimodal architecture that fuses NIR imagery with sparse LiDAR depth and is trained with a physics-constrained dual-head objective. Differentiating through a fixed Koschmieder inversion induces density-adaptive gradient amplification, acting as an implicit resource allocation mechanism that concentrates learning on heavily degraded regions without increasing inference cost. PhysDNet delivers superior restoration with minimal capacity and enhanced training efficiency, facilitating real-time deployment on edge devices without increasing inference overhead. On the Seeing Through Fog benchmark, PhysDNet outperforms competitors by 1.67 dB at 5.2 times lower compute while recovering 54.9% of fog-induced detection loss. Ablations and cross-domain evaluations show that physics-guided training improves generalization, including under non-homogeneous haze that violates the Koschmieder assumption. PhysDNet further demonstrates compatibility with fixed-function NPUs, running at 29/45/99 FPS at <4 W across L/M/S variants. Code, deployment scripts and pre-trained checkpoints are available at this https URL.

AI.tldr: PhysDNet is a lightweight dehazing network that fuses NIR imagery with sparse LiDAR depth and trains with a physics-constrained dual-head objective built on a Koschmieder inversion. It outperforms competitors by 1.67 dB at 5.2 times lower compute and runs at 29, 45 or 99 FPS below 4 W on NPUs.
AI.motivation: Modern dehazing networks are computationally expensive and overfit to synthetic haze, which limits real-time deployment on resource-constrained edge devices.
AI.method: Differentiating through a fixed Koschmieder inversion induces density-adaptive gradient amplification, which concentrates learning on heavily degraded regions without extra inference cost. The network is trained with a physics-constrained dual-head objective.
AI.result: On the Seeing Through Fog benchmark PhysDNet outperforms competitors by 1.67 dB at 5.2 times lower compute and recovers 54.9% of fog-induced detection loss. Ablations and cross-domain tests show that physics-guided training improves generalisation, including under non-homogeneous haze. It runs at 29, 45 and 99 FPS across L, M and S variants at under 4 W on fixed-function NPUs.
AI.conclusion: Physics-guided training gives efficient and generalising restoration suitable for real-time edge deployment without added inference overhead.

title: Vision Language Models for Primary Structure Threat Identification in Wildland Urban Interface Fires
comment: 6 pages, 3 figures, 1 table. Accepted at the 2026 IEEE International Smart Cities Conference (ISC2), Porto, Portugal
summary: Wildland urban interface (WUI) fires increasingly threaten communities and infrastructure, motivating the need for rapid visual assessment. Recent research has focused primarily on detecting fire and assessing post-event damage. However, structure-level fire threat identification during active WUI fire events remains underexplored. This study evaluates Qwen3-VL-8B-Instruct for this active-fire decision using two separately scored tracks: 1,824 synthetic images from 491 designed WUI scenarios and 45 frames from a controlled-burn experiment conducted in collaboration with Columbus Fire & EMS Department. Under zero-shot prompting, the model returned valid target fields for 1,808 synthetic images and 39 controlled-burn frames. Accuracy among valid outputs was 94.0% for the synthetic track and 69.2% for the controlled-burn track, compared with a 16.0% random-selection baseline for the latter. On the synthetic track, the model generally identified the intended target across varied designed WUI scenarios when the relevant fire-spread cues were visually distinct. Controlled-burn performance was well above random selection, but errors showed difficulty interpreting spatial relations in complex scenes. The dual-track protocol provides scalable stress testing in designed scenarios and a controlled-burn reference for assessing model behavior under physical fire conditions. Future work can use the synthetic data for VLM post-training and then evaluate the adapted models on larger and more diverse real WUI fire datasets.

AI.tldr: The paper evaluates Qwen3-VL-8B-Instruct in zero-shot mode for identifying which structure is threatened during active wildland urban interface fires, using a synthetic track and a controlled-burn track. Accuracy among valid outputs is 94.0% on synthetic images and 69.2% on controlled-burn frames, against a 16.0% random baseline for the latter.
AI.motivation: Rapid visual assessment of wildland urban interface fires is needed, but prior work has focused on fire detection and post-event damage rather than structure-level threat identification during active fires.
AI.method: The model is scored on two separate tracks: 1,824 synthetic images from 491 designed WUI scenarios, and 45 frames from a controlled-burn experiment with Columbus Fire and EMS Department. Under zero-shot prompting it returned valid target fields for 1,808 synthetic images and 39 controlled-burn frames.
AI.result: Accuracy among valid outputs is 94.0% on the synthetic track and 69.2% on the controlled-burn track, compared with a 16.0% random-selection baseline. The model identifies intended targets when fire-spread cues are visually distinct, but errors on complex scenes show difficulty with spatial relations.
AI.conclusion: The dual-track protocol offers scalable stress testing with synthetic scenarios and a physical reference, and the synthetic data may support future VLM post-training.

title: RefineSplat: Reconstruction-Guided Object-Centric Gaussian Splatting for Open-Vocabulary Querying
summary: Open-vocabulary 3D scene understanding aims to segment and retrieve arbitrary objects in 3D scenes using natural language queries. Most existing methods typically follow a splat-then-segment paradigm, where 3D Gaussian Splatting is first reconstructed and then augmented with labels or language features for subsequent segmentation. However, this pipeline often suffers from view inconsistency, ambiguous object boundaries, and weak object-level correspondence, especially in complex static and dynamic scenes. Building on our prior Segment-then-Splat framework, we present RefineSplat, a reconstruction-guided extension that retains its object-centric paradigm: it first tracks objects in 2D and then reconstructs each object with a dedicated set of 3D Gaussians, preserving explicit object-Gaussian correspondence for unified open-vocabulary segmentation and retrieval. To improve robustness, we further close the loop between 2D tracking and 3D reconstruction. Since off-the-shelf video trackers can produce unreliable masks that propagate errors into object reconstruction, we introduce a reconstruction-guided feedback mechanism that refines object tracking using rendered masks and multi-view consistency. Moreover, instead of assigning each object a single language embedding, we propose a viewpoint-aware embedding assignment strategy, where each object maintains multiple view-clustered embeddings to capture view-dependent semantic cues. We also introduce Blender-OVS, a synthetic benchmark of static and dynamic sequences with exact object meshes and point clouds, enabling direct evaluation of extracted geometry. Experiments on static and dynamic benchmarks show improved rendered-view segmentation and lower object-level Chamfer distances, with competitive scene reconstruction quality.

AI.tldr: RefineSplat extends an object-centric Segment-then-Splat framework for open-vocabulary 3D querying, adding a feedback loop that refines 2D object tracks using rendered masks and multi-view consistency. It also assigns each object several view-clustered language embeddings and introduces Blender-OVS, a synthetic benchmark with exact object meshes.
AI.motivation: Splat-then-segment pipelines suffer from view inconsistency, ambiguous object boundaries and weak object-level correspondence, especially in complex static and dynamic scenes, and unreliable video-tracker masks propagate errors into reconstruction.
AI.method: Objects are first tracked in 2D and then reconstructed with dedicated 3D Gaussians, preserving explicit object-Gaussian correspondence. A reconstruction-guided feedback mechanism refines tracking using rendered masks and multi-view consistency. A viewpoint-aware embedding assignment gives each object multiple view-clustered embeddings instead of one.
AI.result: Experiments on static and dynamic benchmarks show improved rendered-view segmentation and lower object-level Chamfer distances, with competitive scene reconstruction quality. The abstract reports no specific numbers.
AI.conclusion: Closing the loop between 2D tracking and 3D reconstruction, together with view-dependent embeddings, gives more robust unified open-vocabulary segmentation and retrieval.

title: From Reflection to Co-Evolution: Self-Evolving Agents with Locally Verified Memory
summary: LLM agents have made impressive progress in coding and mathematical reasoning, motivating growing interest in learning from long-horizon interaction. Memory supports this process, but plausible lessons can be redundant or reinforce inappropriate actions. Can a memory's source decision provide a practical test for whether to retain it? We localize consequential trajectory steps, extract candidate memories, and replay each source decision with and without its candidate under the same context. This reveals two properties: most candidates barely shift the probed distribution, and both successful and failed source actions can be reinforced or suppressed. These observations motivate Anchor, which tests shift magnitude and source-role alignment before retention. Admitted memories guide later trajectories, enabling experience-driven improvement under a frozen policy. On held-out ALFWorld and WebShop tasks, Anchor improves success rate and mean score by up to 19.9% and 17.2%, respectively, relative to the strongest baseline for each backbone. With Qwen3.5-27B, it retains 41% fewer ALFWorld cards than unfiltered retention and outperforms all four WebShop cost-comparison baselines while using fewer tokens.

AI.tldr: The paper proposes Anchor, which admits a memory for an LLM agent only if replaying its source decision with and without the candidate shows a meaningful, role-aligned shift in the policy distribution. On held-out ALFWorld and WebShop tasks it improves success rate and mean score by up to 19.9% and 17.2% over the strongest baseline per backbone.
AI.motivation: Memories extracted from long-horizon agent trajectories can be redundant or can reinforce inappropriate actions, so a practical test for whether to retain a memory is needed.
AI.method: Consequential trajectory steps are localised, candidate memories are extracted, and each source decision is replayed with and without its candidate under the same context. Anchor tests shift magnitude and source-role alignment before retention, and admitted memories guide later trajectories under a frozen policy.
AI.result: Anchor improves success rate and mean score by up to 19.9% and 17.2% over the strongest baseline per backbone on ALFWorld and WebShop. With Qwen3.5-27B it retains 41% fewer ALFWorld cards than unfiltered retention and beats all four WebShop cost-comparison baselines while using fewer tokens.
AI.conclusion: Replay-based verification of memories is a practical way to make experience-driven agent improvement more selective and token-efficient, without updating the policy.

title: Tiresias: Towards Language-Conditioned World Models
comment: 33 pages, including appendix and references. Code: this https URL
summary: World models enable planning through internal simulation, while natural language provides intuitive task specification. Yet, language-conditioned world modeling remains fragmented across domains with disparate action spaces, datasets, and evaluation protocols. We introduce LCWM, a shared task that maps an initial agent-view observation and a language instruction to an action sequence that fulfills the instruction. Its accompanying benchmark, LCWM-Bench, integrates 15 datasets across navigation, robotics, 3D gaming, and driving under a shared action interface and evaluation protocol, pairing 142,987 episodes with 428,961 instructions in three styles. We further propose Tiresias, an agent that plans via selective imagination: a language-conditioned diffusion policy generates candidate trajectories, a trajectory ranker shortlists them, and a video-pretrained world model imagines their visual consequences. A visual ranker evaluates these rollouts, complementing trajectory scores to select the final plan. Tiresias achieves competitive planning and imagination performance on LCWM-Bench. Ablations demonstrate the complementary benefits of trajectory ranking and visual verification, while experiments with alternative proposal methods show that the trained rankers remain effective beyond our diffusion policy. Together, LCWM-Bench and Tiresias provide a unified evaluation setting and an effective starting point for studying language-guided planning through world models.

AI.tldr: The paper introduces LCWM, a shared task and the LCWM-Bench benchmark mapping an observation and a language instruction to an action sequence across 15 datasets, and proposes Tiresias, a planner that combines a language-conditioned diffusion policy, a trajectory ranker and a video-pretrained world model. Tiresias achieves competitive planning and imagination performance on LCWM-Bench.
AI.motivation: Language-conditioned world modelling is fragmented across domains with different action spaces, datasets and evaluation protocols, so the field lacks a common task and benchmark.
AI.method: LCWM-Bench integrates 15 datasets spanning navigation, robotics, 3D gaming and driving under a shared action interface and evaluation protocol, with 142,987 episodes and 428,961 instructions in three styles. Tiresias generates candidate trajectories with a diffusion policy, shortlists them with a trajectory ranker, imagines their visual consequences with a world model, and selects the final plan with a visual ranker.
AI.result: Tiresias achieves competitive planning and imagination performance on LCWM-Bench. Ablations show complementary benefits of trajectory ranking and visual verification, and the trained rankers remain effective with alternative proposal methods.
AI.conclusion: LCWM-Bench and Tiresias together provide a unified evaluation setting and a starting point for studying language-guided planning through world models.

title: Frequency-Structure Complementary Modeling for Hyperspectral Image Fusion
summary: Existing methods mainly rely on convolutional aggregation or attention-based spatial-spectral interaction. However, conventional feature-domain attention does not explicitly characterize variation patterns along spatial-token and learned latent-channel coordinates, while spatially shared local operators lack the flexibility to adapt neighborhood aggregation to heterogeneous structures. To address these limitations, we propose a Frequency-Structure Complementary Modeling Network (FSCM-Net), which couples frequency-aware dependency learning with structure-adaptive local refinement. Specifically, a Spatial-Spectral Frequency Calibration Attention (SSFCA) module constructs spatial-token affinities from Fourier-interacted query-key representations and builds latent-channel affinities after input-conditioned frequency filtering along learned channel coordinates. The latent-channel response is then calibrated by a learned shared gain and combined with the spatial-token response. Complementarily, a Structure-Coherent Dynamic Feature Fusion (SC-DFF) module combines regularized structure-tensor cues from MSI features with context-modulated HSI detail representations to generate channel- and position-dependent aggregation kernels. This design makes local HSI refinement responsive to smooth regions, edges, and textures while maintaining spectral fidelity. The two modules are progressively integrated within a multiscale encoder-decoder to coordinate representation-level interaction and structure-adaptive reconstruction. Experiments on two simulated benchmarks and one real remote-sensing dataset demonstrate favorable performance against representative fusion methods in spatial detail reconstruction and spectral preservation.

AI.tldr: The paper proposes FSCM-Net, a hyperspectral image fusion network that combines frequency-aware dependency learning with structure-adaptive local refinement, and reports favorable spatial detail and spectral preservation on two simulated benchmarks and one real remote-sensing dataset.
AI.motivation: Existing fusion methods rely on convolutional aggregation or attention, but conventional feature-domain attention does not explicitly model variation along spatial-token and latent-channel coordinates, and spatially shared local operators cannot adapt neighborhood aggregation to heterogeneous structures.
AI.method: SSFCA builds spatial-token affinities from Fourier-interacted query-key representations and latent-channel affinities after input-conditioned frequency filtering, then calibrates the channel response with a learned shared gain; SC-DFF fuses regularized structure-tensor cues from MSI features with context-modulated HSI details to produce channel- and position-dependent aggregation kernels; both are integrated in a multiscale encoder-decoder.
AI.result: FSCM-Net shows favorable performance against representative fusion methods on two simulated benchmarks and one real remote-sensing dataset in spatial detail reconstruction and spectral preservation; the abstract gives no numeric values.
AI.conclusion: Coupling frequency-aware global dependency modeling with structure-adaptive local refinement is presented as an effective design for hyperspectral image fusion that keeps spectral fidelity while responding to smooth regions, edges and textures.

title: S2HAND: Accuracy-Preservation Trade-Offs for Hand Specialization in Whole-Body Pose Models
comment: 39 pages, including appendices. Code and models: this https URL
summary: Unified whole-body pose estimators jointly predict body, face, and hand landmarks, but often degrade on small, blurred, or occluded hands. Attaching a standalone hand specialist introduces extra detection overhead, coordinate alignment, and wrist-stitching artifacts. We introduce S2HAND, a hand-specialized Sapiens2-5B framework that preserves the native 308-keypoint output interface. Specifically, S2HAND-MT adapts a lightweight 0.87M-parameter pose branch to route 40 finger heatmaps while strictly preserving the shared Transformer, auxiliary task heads, and the other 268 body, foot, and face heatmaps. S2HAND-Pose further fine-tunes three Fisher-selected Transformer blocks (267.13M parameters), trading exact preservation for stronger hand recovery: it lifts macro AUC from 57.83% to 65.73% across HInt TEST, COCO WholeBody VAL, and FreiHAND EVAL, and surpasses HInt-adapted Hand5/HRNet and stitched Hand5 systems on all five Native Pipeline benchmarks. On COCO, S2HAND-Pose improves hand AP by 12.89 points and body-plus-foot AP by 0.19 points. Across a 512-image multi-task audit, it maintains 99.60% foreground segmentation agreement with the public checkpoint, with quantified normal and pointmap drift. Its 2D coordinates also lower 3D mesh error in frozen Pose2Mesh transfer, while our optional TailGuard re-cropping module cuts S2HAND-MT's severe failure rate on NewDays from 13.45% to 10.43%. S2HAND thus resolves the whole-body hand bottleneck with either exact non-hand preservation (MT) or empirically audited trade-offs (Pose).

AI.tldr: S2HAND specializes the Sapiens2-5B whole-body pose model for hands, with a variant that keeps the native 308-keypoint interface and non-hand outputs exact, and a variant that fine-tunes Transformer blocks for stronger hand recovery at the cost of exact preservation.
AI.motivation: Unified whole-body pose estimators degrade on small, blurred or occluded hands, and attaching a standalone hand specialist adds detection overhead, coordinate alignment problems and wrist-stitching artifacts.
AI.method: S2HAND-MT adds a lightweight 0.87M-parameter pose branch that routes 40 finger heatmaps while keeping the shared Transformer, auxiliary heads and the other 268 body, foot and face heatmaps unchanged; S2HAND-Pose fine-tunes three Fisher-selected Transformer blocks (267.13M parameters); an optional TailGuard re-cropping module is also evaluated.
AI.result: S2HAND-Pose raises macro AUC from 57.83% to 65.73% across HInt TEST, COCO WholeBody VAL and FreiHAND EVAL and beats HInt-adapted Hand5/HRNet and stitched Hand5 on all five Native Pipeline benchmarks; on COCO it improves hand AP by 12.89 points and body-plus-foot AP by 0.19 points; S2HAND-MT keeps 99.60% foreground segmentation agreement with the public checkpoint; TailGuard lowers the severe failure rate of S2HAND-MT on NewDays from 13.45% to 10.43%.
AI.conclusion: The hand bottleneck of whole-body pose can be addressed either with exact non-hand preservation (MT) or with empirically audited trade-offs (Pose), and the 2D improvements also reduce 3D mesh error in frozen Pose2Mesh transfer.

title: Mental Imagery That Matters: Curing Latent Collapse in Multimodal Reasoning
comment: Accepted by NeurIPS 2026, Project page: this https URL
summary: Mental simulation, the ability to reason by constructing and updating internal visual states, is central to flexible human cognition, but remains elusive in current multimodal large language models. Latent multimodal reasoning offers a promising route toward this capability by interleaving text with continuous visual latent blocks, allowing models to maintain internal visual workspaces without decoding them into pixels. In this paper, we ask whether these latent visual states actually matter. Through a direct perturbation analysis across representative latent-reasoning MLLMs, we find that they often do not: dropping, replacing, or shuffling generated visual latents has only minor effects on the model's own final-answer probability, while equivalent perturbations to the linguistic reasoning trace are substantially more damaging. We call this failure mode Mental Simulation Collapse (MSC): the model appears to perform interleaved visual reasoning, but routes most answer-relevant computation through text. We further diagnose that MSC follows naturally from existing training objectives: visual alignment can make generated latents resemble helper-image embeddings, but it does not require the decoder to rely on them; subsequent text-only supervision further leaves the semantic role of the latent pathway unidentifiable. To address this, we introduce AnchorSim (Anchored Mental Simulation), a contrastive distillation framework that trains models to make their generated visual latents consequential. Across multiple visual reasoning benchmarks, AnchorSim improves performance, while diagnostic re-evaluation shows that visual perturbations now meaningfully affect predictions. Our results expose a fundamental failure mode of latent multimodal reasoning and demonstrate that mental simulation must be anchored to model behavior in order to matter.

AI.tldr: The paper shows that latent-reasoning multimodal LLMs often ignore their generated visual latents, names this Mental Simulation Collapse, and proposes AnchorSim, a contrastive distillation method that makes the latents consequential and improves visual reasoning benchmarks.
AI.motivation: Latent multimodal reasoning is meant to let models maintain internal visual workspaces, but it is unclear whether the visual latents actually affect answers, and existing training objectives do not guarantee that they do.
AI.method: A direct perturbation analysis drops, replaces or shuffles generated visual latents and compares the effect with perturbations of the linguistic trace across representative latent-reasoning MLLMs; the authors diagnose that visual alignment does not force the decoder to use the latents and that text-only supervision leaves their role unidentifiable; AnchorSim is a contrastive distillation framework that trains the generated latents to matter.
AI.result: Perturbing visual latents has only minor effects on final-answer probability while perturbing text is substantially more damaging; AnchorSim improves performance across multiple visual reasoning benchmarks, and re-evaluation shows visual perturbations now meaningfully change predictions; the abstract gives no numeric values.
AI.conclusion: Latent multimodal reasoning can fail by routing answer-relevant computation through text, and mental simulation has to be anchored to model behavior before it contributes to reasoning.

title: Split and Bridge: Multimodal Generation via Diffusion Bridging
summary: Visual data are often expressed through multiple complementary modalities (e.g., images and segmentation masks), each capturing different aspects of the same underlying structure. Most existing multimodal methods adopt a top-down paradigm, learning a shared latent variable through joint training from scratch, which limits scalability. We propose Split and Bridge (SnB), a bottom-up framework for multimodal generation that couples pretrained unimodal diffusion models at sampling time. Rather than learning a unified latent space, SnB generates coherent multimodal samples by following a shared diffusion trajectory up to a split point and then branching into modality-specific trajectories guided by a bridge module. This design enables plug-and-play reuse of powerful pretrained models without joint training, making it scalable and easily adaptable. Across standard benchmarks (PolyMNIST, CelebAMask-HQ) and more complex settings (PIE-Bench++, ROCO), SnB achieves a strong balance between sample quality and coherence. We show that SnB naturally extends to downstream zero-shot tasks such as interleaved co-generation, image editing, and style coupling/decoupling. Our results demonstrate that bottom-up generation provides a practical framework that complements existing top-down multimodal approaches. Code is available at this https URL

AI.tldr: Split and Bridge (SnB) generates multimodal samples by coupling pretrained unimodal diffusion models at sampling time, following a shared trajectory up to a split point and then branching into modality-specific trajectories through a bridge module, without joint training.
AI.motivation: Existing multimodal generators learn a shared latent variable through joint training from scratch, which limits scalability and prevents reuse of strong pretrained unimodal models.
AI.method: The method runs a shared diffusion trajectory until a split point, then branches each modality into its own trajectory guided by a bridge module, so that pretrained unimodal diffusion models are reused in a plug-and-play way.
AI.result: SnB achieves a strong balance between sample quality and coherence on PolyMNIST and CelebAMask-HQ and on the more complex PIE-Bench++ and ROCO settings; it extends zero-shot to interleaved co-generation, image editing and style coupling/decoupling; the abstract gives no numeric values.
AI.conclusion: Bottom-up generation from pretrained unimodal models is presented as a practical framework that complements existing top-down multimodal approaches.

title: ESTRA: Enabling Extreme Attention Sparsity for Training-Free Video Diffusion Acceleration
summary: Video diffusion transformers generate high-quality videos, but attention over long spatiotemporal sequences makes inference computationally expensive. Sparse attention reduces this cost by computing only a subset of query-key interactions exactly, and recent training-free methods further approximate the remaining interactions. These methods, however, degrade quickly at high sparsity, which limits the achievable speedup. We present ESTRA (Extreme Sparsity Through Refined Attention), a training-free acceleration method that preserves generation quality even at extreme sparsity. ESTRA concentrates exact attention computation on a small set of important key-value tokens and approximates the remaining contributions with cluster representatives. To identify these tokens efficiently, it groups similar queries and uses their representatives to score individual keys. A variance-based correction further refines the attention weights of the cluster representatives, improving the accuracy of the approximation. Experiments on Wan2.1-14B and HunyuanVideo-13B show that ESTRA establishes a new quality-efficiency frontier for training-free sparse attention, achieving $3.26\times$ and $4.71\times$ end-to-end speedups at 5% attention density while surpassing Sol-Attn and SVG-EAR in fidelity to dense generation and on most VBench dimensions. Even at 1% density, ESTRA remains more faithful to dense generation than Sol-Attn at 12.5%, while reaching up to $5.39\times$ speedup.

AI.tldr: ESTRA is a training-free sparse attention method for video diffusion transformers that keeps generation quality at extreme sparsity, reporting 3.26x and 4.71x end-to-end speedups at 5% attention density on Wan2.1-14B and HunyuanVideo-13B.
AI.motivation: Attention over long spatiotemporal sequences makes video diffusion inference expensive, and existing training-free sparse attention methods degrade quickly at high sparsity, which limits the achievable speedup.
AI.method: ESTRA computes exact attention on a small set of important key-value tokens and approximates the remaining contributions with cluster representatives; it groups similar queries to score individual keys efficiently, and a variance-based correction refines the attention weights of the cluster representatives.
AI.result: At 5% attention density ESTRA reaches 3.26x and 4.71x end-to-end speedups on Wan2.1-14B and HunyuanVideo-13B while surpassing Sol-Attn and SVG-EAR in fidelity to dense generation and on most VBench dimensions; at 1% density it stays more faithful to dense generation than Sol-Attn at 12.5% and reaches up to 5.39x speedup.
AI.conclusion: ESTRA establishes a new quality-efficiency frontier for training-free sparse attention in video diffusion, showing that extreme sparsity can be used without training.

title: WordEval: Evaluating Word-Native Operation Fidelity in Document Editing
comment: Accepted at NeurIPS 2026 (Evaluations and Datasets Track). Project page with code and data at this https URL
summary: Microsoft Word is a central environment for office automation, and the faithful execution of its editing operations is an important capability for document agents. Unlike plain-text editing, editing in Word modifies a structured object model, where the requested effect is realized in object properties. Existing benchmarks, however, evaluate office workflows or desktop automation, treating word-processor documents as one task domain among many and verifying outcomes with keyword matching, per-task property checks, or screenshot comparison. We introduce WordEval, an operation-fidelity benchmark that instead centers evaluation on Word editing operations, testing whether each requested edit is realized as intended changes to Word objects and properties. It contains 642 cases across 15 Word feature areas, ranging from text and lists to charts, shape geometry, and SmartArt. 546 atomic cases cover 231 commands, 96 compositional cases combine multiple edits in a single document, and a Word-native oracle checks task-specific object properties and preservation conditions. Cases are constructed from editing-unit specifications, yielding controlled input documents, reference documents, and aligned oracle checks. Each compositional case is linked to corresponding atomic cases, supporting fine-grained diagnosis of editing failures. We evaluate eight agent systems and find that many struggle on the Atomic track, with performance varying across feature areas. Moreover, every system scores lower on Compositional than on Atomic, with gaps that vary substantially by system. Exact atomic-intent links and recorded failure diagnoses provide complementary views of this variation.

AI.tldr: WordEval is a benchmark of 642 cases across 15 Word feature areas that tests whether document agents realize each requested editing operation as the intended change to Word objects and properties, rather than only checking outcomes by keywords or screenshots.
AI.motivation: Existing benchmarks treat Word as one task domain among many office workflows and verify outcomes with keyword matching, per-task property checks or screenshot comparison, which does not test whether the structured object model was edited correctly.
AI.method: Cases are built from editing-unit specifications with controlled input documents, reference documents and aligned oracle checks; 546 atomic cases cover 231 commands, 96 compositional cases combine several edits, each linked to its atomic cases, and a Word-native oracle checks object properties and preservation conditions.
AI.result: Eight agent systems are evaluated; many struggle on the Atomic track with performance varying across feature areas, and every system scores lower on Compositional than on Atomic, with gaps that differ substantially by system.
AI.conclusion: Atomic-intent links and recorded failure diagnoses give complementary views of where Word editing fails, and the benchmark supports fine-grained diagnosis of document agents.

title: They Can See It but Not Say It: Iterative Self Knowledge Re-expression in Visual Reasoning Relative Pose Identification
summary: The task of visual reasoning relative pose identification (VRRPI) has exposed critical weaknesses in the multi-view 3D spatial reasoning capabilities of modern vision-language models (VLMs). We present a systematic analysis of VLMs' behavior in VRRPI, uncovering stable output biases where VLMs disproportionately predict specific motion patterns regardless of visual evidence. To mitigate these inherent biases, we propose self knowledge re-expression with iterative debiasing (SKR-ID), an annotation-free pipeline that adapts VLMs for VRRPI using only randomly extracted unannotated image pairs. SKR-ID transitions VLMs' output mechanism from generic next-token prediction to task-optimized classification heads. The pipeline proceeds in two stages: (1) a cold-start initialization using debiasing object-centric prompts to anchor motion inference in 2D visual evidence; and (2) a recursive logit-ranking mechanism that enforces statistical parity by using the median logit value as a dynamic threshold. Experimental evaluation across frontier VLMs on standard benchmarks demonstrates that SKR-ID significantly mitigates systematic biases. Our method improves open-source VLMs' Macro-F1 scores from 35.0-45.4% to 53.7-58.0%, without using any annotated data. These results show that SKR-ID can effectively improve 3D reasoning performance from a severely collapsed baseline. The code is publicly available at this https URL.

AI.tldr: The paper finds that vision-language models have stable output biases on visual reasoning relative pose identification and proposes SKR-ID, an annotation-free pipeline that adapts VLMs with unannotated image pairs to reduce these biases and raise Macro-F1.
AI.motivation: Modern VLMs show weak multi-view 3D spatial reasoning, with systematic predictions of specific motion patterns regardless of visual evidence, and existing adaptation requires annotated data.
AI.method: SKR-ID has two stages: a cold-start initialization using debiasing object-centric prompts to anchor motion inference in 2D visual evidence, and a recursive logit-ranking mechanism that enforces statistical parity by using the median logit as a dynamic threshold, which turns the output mechanism into task-optimized classification heads.
AI.result: On standard benchmarks SKR-ID raises the Macro-F1 of open-source VLMs from 35.0-45.4% to 53.7-58.0% without any annotated data, and significantly mitigates systematic biases across frontier VLMs.
AI.conclusion: Self knowledge re-expression can improve 3D reasoning from a severely collapsed baseline without annotations.

title: Can General-Purpose Generative AI Supply Training Data for Medical Vision Models? A Multimodal Retrospective Study
summary: Background: Well-annotated, diverse medical imaging datasets remain a major constraint for vision-based medical AI. We evaluated Nano Banana, a general-purpose image generation and editing model, as a source of synthetic medical images for model training, subgroup augmentation, and model auditing. Methods: In this retrospective study across four imaging modalities, chest radiography, fundus photography, and CT models were trained only on synthetic images and externally validated on real-world data against real-data-trained models. Carotid ultrasound models were trained on a private Human Phenotype Project cohort (aged 40-75 years) with and without synthetic augmentation. Clinicians rated image plausibility. Evaluation used AUROC, AUPR, calibration, and decision curve analysis. Findings: Synthetic-only models achieved AUROCs of 0.877 (95% CI 0.843-0.910) for pneumonia (n=14863), 0.963 (0.948-0.975) for retinal detachment (n=1149), and 0.711 (0.600-0.823) for renal calculus (n=4122), comparable to real-data-trained models, but their calibration and net benefit were not consistently more favorable. With mixed synthetic-real training, a carotid ultrasound model produced an ordinal vascular age index that stratified 633 external subjects into subgroups differing in BMI and glucose (both p<0.01), linking vascular aging to cardiometabolic health. To stress-test shortcut learning, editing a moderate tessellated pattern into fundus photographs reduced the true-class probability for central serous chorioretinopathy from 0.996 to 0.822. Clinician-guided editing raised low-quality CT plausibility from 3.10/5 to 4.30/5. Interpretation: Synthetic data can complement real data in model training, subgroup representation, and model testing via controlled editing, but its clinical value should be assessed with calibration, decision curve analysis, and clinician review, not discrimination alone.

AI.tldr: In a retrospective multi-modality study, the general-purpose image model Nano Banana produced synthetic medical images that trained models comparable to real-data models for some tasks, but synthetic data did not consistently improve calibration or net benefit, so clinical value needs calibration, decision curve analysis and clinician review.
AI.motivation: Well-annotated, diverse medical imaging datasets are a major constraint for vision-based medical AI, and it is unclear whether a general-purpose generative model can supply usable training data, subgroup augmentation and model auditing.
AI.method: Models were trained only on synthetic chest radiograph, fundus and CT images and externally validated on real data against real-data models; carotid ultrasound models were trained on a private Human Phenotype Project cohort with and without synthetic augmentation; clinicians rated plausibility, and evaluation used AUROC, AUPR, calibration and decision curve analysis; controlled editing was used for shortcut stress tests.
AI.result: Synthetic-only models reached AUROCs of 0.877 for pneumonia (n=14863), 0.963 for retinal detachment (n=1149) and 0.711 for renal calculus (n=4122), comparable to real-data models; a mixed-training carotid ultrasound model produced a vascular age index that stratified 633 external subjects by BMI and glucose (both p<0.01); editing a tessellated pattern into fundus photographs lowered the true-class probability for central serous chorioretinopathy from 0.996 to 0.822; clinician-guided editing raised low-quality CT plausibility from 3.10/5 to 4.30/5.
AI.conclusion: Synthetic data can complement real data for training, subgroup representation and controlled model testing, but its clinical value should not be judged by discrimination alone.

title: Decoupling Direction and Magnitude: Language-Steered Flow Matching for Super-Resolution in the Dark
comment: Accepted at NeurIPS 2026 (poster). 32 pages, 12 figures, and 13 tables. Code and pretrained models: this https URL
summary: Image super-resolution in the dark is fundamentally challenged by extreme spatial heterogeneity: severely underexposed and noisy regions demand aggressive generative enhancement to reconstruct missing details, while relatively well-exposed areas require conservative updates to prevent hallucinated textures. Standard diffusion and flow-matching models, however, rely on globally uniform integration trajectories, making them sub-optimal for such spatially varying degradations. In this paper, we propose DeLang-SR (Degradation-Language steered Super-Resolution), a one-step flow-matching framework that explicitly decouples the restoration direction and magnitude. Rather than treating low-light corruption as arbitrary latent features, DeLang-SR translates measurable physical statistics into structured degradation language, harnessing the semantic prior of pretrained text-to-image models. The degradation-language intent, complemented by image-specific visual tokens, steers the velocity field (direction) toward restoration-relevant manifolds. Simultaneously, a continuous spatial update-strength field acts as a locally varying Euler step-size field (magnitude), applying stronger integration steps in heavily degraded shadows while enforcing conservative updates in reliable regions. Experiments on paired and real dark images, together with ablations and diagnostic analyses, show that DeLang-SR provides an effective and interpretable one-step route to super-resolution in the dark. Code and pretrained models are available at this https URL.

AI.tldr: DeLang-SR is a one-step flow-matching framework for super-resolution of dark images that separates restoration direction, steered by degradation-language prompts, from magnitude, controlled by a spatial update-strength field that acts as a locally varying Euler step size.
AI.motivation: Underexposed and noisy regions need aggressive generative reconstruction while well-exposed regions need conservative updates, but standard diffusion and flow-matching models use globally uniform integration trajectories that suit spatially varying degradation poorly.
AI.method: Physical image statistics are translated into structured degradation language that exploits the semantic prior of a pretrained text-to-image model; together with image-specific visual tokens, this language steers the velocity field, while a continuous spatial update-strength field sets local integration step sizes.
AI.result: Experiments on paired and real dark images, with ablations and diagnostic analyses, show an effective and interpretable one-step route to super-resolution in the dark; the abstract gives no numeric values.
AI.conclusion: Decoupling direction from magnitude gives an interpretable one-step alternative for super-resolution under extreme low light.

title: Disentangling Channel Semantics in Vision Transformers via Token Decorrelation and Composition-Aware Modulation
summary: Multi-channel images encode heterogeneous channel semantics aligned over a shared spatial structure, which requires models to jointly capture globally shared structure and channel-specific variations. Recent multi-channel Vision Transformers attempt to address this challenge by augmenting the [CLS] token with memory tokens to organize multi-channel representations under varying channel compositions. However, we find that these context tokens collapse onto a few dominant channels under high inter-channel redundancy, producing redundant representations and a biased global summary that fails to reliably support composition-aware channel interpretation. We propose MuCa-ViT (Multi-Channel Composition-Aware Vision Transformer), a unified framework that addresses these limitations through two coupled mechanisms. Factorial Token Learning (FTL) enforces token-level decorrelation among context tokens, encouraging the [CLS] token to capture globally shared semantics while memory tokens preserve complementary channel-specific cues. Channel Composition-Aware Modulation (CAM) uses the FTL-refined [CLS] as a semantic anchor to generate sample-wise modulation signals, which enable composition-aware interpretation of channels within a unified backbone rather than relying on static channel embeddings. Experiments on JUMP-CP, CHAMMI, and So2Sat show that MuCa-ViT outperforms prior multi-channel ViTs across all three benchmarks, and the magnitude of improvement aligns with the inter-channel redundancy of each dataset ($\rho \in [0.19, 0.77]$), validating the diagnostic analysis that motivates our design. Our code is available at this https URL .

AI.tldr: MuCa-ViT addresses channel collapse in multi-channel Vision Transformers by decorrelating context tokens so the [CLS] token captures shared semantics and by generating sample-wise channel modulation from that anchor, improving over prior multi-channel ViTs on JUMP-CP, CHAMMI and So2Sat.
AI.motivation: Memory-token augmentation of the [CLS] token in multi-channel ViTs collapses onto a few dominant channels under high inter-channel redundancy, which yields redundant representations and a biased global summary.
AI.method: Factorial Token Learning (FTL) enforces token-level decorrelation among context tokens so that [CLS] carries globally shared semantics while memory tokens keep channel-specific cues; Channel Composition-Aware Modulation (CAM) uses the refined [CLS] as a semantic anchor to produce sample-wise modulation signals in place of static channel embeddings.
AI.result: MuCa-ViT outperforms prior multi-channel ViTs on JUMP-CP, CHAMMI and So2Sat, and the size of the gain tracks each dataset's inter-channel redundancy (rho between 0.19 and 0.77); the abstract gives no further numeric values.
AI.conclusion: Explicit decorrelation of context tokens combined with composition-aware modulation yields more reliable global summaries and channel interpretation in a unified backbone.

title: SRA: Spatial Reasoning Adapter via Evolving Social Interaction Graphs for Trajectory Prediction
summary: Predicting where multiple agents will move next is fundamental to autonomous driving, robotics, and any system that must share space with people safely. Modern stochastic predictors read off inter-agent interactions once from the observed past and keep that view fixed throughout the generative rollout, so the reciprocal geometric constraints that emerge as the joint future sharpens are not re-examined. We address this gap with SRA (Spatial Reasoning Adapter), a modular graph denoiser that is integrated into existing diffusion and flow-matching predictors without redesigning their generative cores. At every reverse step, SRA reads the host's current future estimate, builds a sparse Euclidean interaction graph on the predicted trajectories, and returns a residual correction to the host's decoding path. Our adapter consists of three core components: a sparse neighborhood retrieved with a learned query-key score and a geometric bias, a future-conditioned relational feature recomputed on the evolving prediction, and uncertainty-weighted message passing where confident agents act as anchors for uncertain ones. We instantiate SRA on three structurally different hosts (LED, MID, and MoFlow) across four multi-agent benchmarks: SDD, NBA, Soccer, and Football. SRA improves ADE for every host on every dataset, with average gains of 5.8% in ADE and 7.0% in FDE. A cumulative ablation shows that the three components act as one mechanism: only together do they improve every host on every sports dataset, indicating that spatial reasoning over the model's own evolving future, weighted by how far that future can be trusted, is broadly useful across denoising architectures. Code is available at this https URL.

AI.tldr: SRA is a modular graph denoiser that plugs into existing diffusion and flow-matching trajectory predictors and re-reads inter-agent interactions at every reverse step, improving ADE for every host on every dataset with average gains of 5.8% ADE and 7.0% FDE.
AI.motivation: Stochastic trajectory predictors compute inter-agent interactions once from the observed past and keep them fixed through generation, so the reciprocal geometric constraints that emerge as the joint future sharpens are never re-examined.
AI.method: At each reverse step SRA builds a sparse Euclidean interaction graph on the current predicted trajectories and returns a residual correction; it combines a sparse neighborhood retrieved by a learned query-key score with a geometric bias, a future-conditioned relational feature recomputed on the evolving prediction, and uncertainty-weighted message passing in which confident agents anchor uncertain ones.
AI.result: SRA is instantiated on LED, MID and MoFlow across SDD, NBA, Soccer and Football, improving ADE for every host on every dataset with average gains of 5.8% in ADE and 7.0% in FDE; a cumulative ablation shows the three components help every host on every sports dataset only when combined.
AI.conclusion: Spatial reasoning over the model's own evolving future, weighted by its trustworthiness, is broadly useful across denoising architectures for trajectory prediction.

title: Scaling Optimization-Oriented Hypernetworks for Implicit Neural Representations
comment: 33 pages, including appendices. Code: this https URL
summary: We present a hypernetwork that generates the parameters of an implicit neural representation (INR) for a given signal in a single forward pass, without test-time optimization. Existing hypernetworks for this problem either ignore the chain-rule structure of the test-time optimization that produces an INR or, when they preserve it, instantiate the structure with MLPs whose parameter count grows quartically in target-network width. Our central contribution is to show that this parameter-count cost is structural to the MLP instantiation, not to the optimization-oriented principle of preserving chain-rule structure, and to resolve it by replacing the MLP body with attention. The resulting hypernetwork combines three design choices: an output-neuron-centric tokenization that aligns the token axis with each layer's output-neuron axis; an information-flow consistency rule that fixes the role of every cross-attention module from the representation its output should occupy; and a token-space iterative rollout that realizes the five quantities one optimization step on the target INR computes as five cross-attention modules with parameter count independent of target-network width. Across five 2D and 3D INR generation benchmarks, our method outperforms the state-of-the-art single-pass and optimization-oriented baselines; scales to target-network widths at which the MLP-based optimization-oriented paradigm exhausts GPU memory; and produces the highest result on NeRF generation without ground-truth INR weights supervision.

AI.tldr: The paper presents a hypernetwork that generates implicit neural representation parameters in one forward pass while preserving the chain-rule structure of test-time optimization, by replacing the MLP body with attention so that the parameter count does not grow quartically with target-network width.
AI.motivation: Prior hypernetworks either ignore the chain-rule structure of INR optimization or, when they keep it using MLPs, incur a parameter count that grows quartically with target-network width.
AI.method: The hypernetwork uses output-neuron-centric tokenization that aligns tokens with each layer's output neurons, an information-flow consistency rule that fixes the role of each cross-attention module, and a token-space iterative rollout in which the five quantities of one optimization step are computed by five cross-attention modules whose parameter count is independent of target width.
AI.result: Across five 2D and 3D INR generation benchmarks the method outperforms single-pass and optimization-oriented baselines, scales to target widths where MLP-based optimization-oriented hypernetworks run out of GPU memory, and gives the highest result on NeRF generation without ground-truth INR weight supervision.
AI.conclusion: The width-induced parameter cost comes from the MLP instantiation rather than from preserving chain-rule structure, so attention can keep the optimization-oriented principle while scaling.

title: Beyond Row Alignment: Virtual-Camera-Aware Online Stereo Rectification
summary: Stereo matchers estimate depth by comparing the left and right images from a stereo camera pair, but they assume that the two cameras are accurately calibrated and rectified. In real deployments, small physical shifts after calibration, caused by camera motion, mechanical drift, vibration, or installation changes, can break this assumption and degrade depth estimation. Online stereo rectification is therefore needed to correct the image pair during operation and recover a stereo geometry where standard stereo matching can work reliably. Recent online rectification methods mainly optimize row alignment, making the left and right views of the same scene point fall on the same image row. We show that this target, while necessary, is insufficient for deployable stereo depth estimation. A rectifier may make a small set of matched points look well row-aligned, but still distort the full images in ways that hurt stereo matching: useful image regions may be cut off, large blank areas may appear, objects may be stretched or squeezed, or image scale may change unevenly across the view. We propose VirtualRect, an online stereo rectification method designed for reliable real-world deployment. Rather than treating rectification as simply making the left and right image rows line up, this method estimates a rectified virtual stereo camera and combines image-wide supervision of image warp behavior. This makes the rectified images and the camera parameters come from the same geometry, so the images used for matching and the model used for depth computation remain consistent. Experiments on multiple datasets show that, compared with the prior state-of-the-art online rectifier, VirtualRect reduces vertical flow error by 17% on Carla-Flowguided and 7% on Semi-Truck Highway, and lowers depth MAE by 30-41% on Carla-Flowguided across three downstream stereo matchers.

AI.tldr: VirtualRect is an online stereo rectifier that estimates a rectified virtual stereo camera and supervises the full-image warp behavior, not only row alignment, reducing vertical flow error and depth MAE relative to the prior state-of-the-art online rectifier.
AI.motivation: Recent online rectification methods mainly optimize row alignment, which is necessary but insufficient, because a rectifier can align a few matched points while cutting off image content, creating blank regions, or distorting scale.
AI.method: VirtualRect estimates a rectified virtual stereo camera so that the rectified images and camera parameters come from the same geometry, and combines image-wide supervision of warp behavior so that the images used for matching and the model used for depth remain consistent.
AI.result: Compared with the prior state-of-the-art online rectifier, VirtualRect reduces vertical flow error by 17% on Carla-Flowguided and 7% on Semi-Truck Highway, and lowers depth MAE by 30-41% on Carla-Flowguided across three downstream stereo matchers.
AI.conclusion: Deployable stereo depth needs rectification that treats the whole image and the virtual camera geometry, not just row alignment of matched points.

title: PrivMark: Pixel-Space Steering against Privacy Leakage in Vision-Language Models
summary: Vision-language models (VLMs) routinely disclose soft-biometric attributes such as age, gender, and race in their text outputs, exposing demographic information from uploaded images to any downstream API user. Existing privacy defenses do not fit this setting: face de-identification leaves distributed soft-biometric cues intact, classifier-targeted adversarial perturbations do not transfer to open-ended generation, and stronger VLM-specific methods require retraining or runtime activation access unavailable to downstream APIs. We propose PrivMark, a framework that suppresses biometric leakage at the image level. By analyzing VLM activations, we identify two weakly aligned steering vector directions in hidden-state space, each tied to a distinct leakage behavior --- one corresponding to incidental attribute disclosure under open-ended descriptions, the other to compliance with direct biometric probes instead of refusal --- and encode both directions into a single bounded pixel perturbation, so the protected image alone enforces privacy with no invasive access to model internals at deployment. To support evaluation, we assemble BioleakBench, $1{,}600$ VQA pairs covering biometric privacy attributes under both free-form description and direct-probe protocols. Across three white-box source models, PrivMark achieves up to $85.9\%$ biometric suppression while retaining $75\%$ of clean OK-VQA utility, up to $1.4\times$ the privacy-utility tradeoff of the strongest pixel-only baseline. The same one-shot perturbations transfer consistently to seven unseen VLMs including closed-source APIs.

AI.tldr: PrivMark is an image-level defense that adds one bounded pixel perturbation encoding two steering directions from VLM activations, suppressing soft-biometric leakage such as age, gender and race in open-ended descriptions and direct probes, and transferring to unseen VLMs including closed-source APIs.
AI.motivation: VLMs disclose soft-biometric attributes from uploaded images, while face de-identification leaves distributed cues intact, classifier-targeted adversarial perturbations do not transfer to open-ended generation, and stronger VLM-specific methods need retraining or activation access that downstream API users lack.
AI.method: Two weakly aligned steering directions in hidden-state space are identified from VLM activations, one tied to incidental attribute disclosure and one to compliance with direct biometric probes instead of refusal; both are encoded into a single bounded pixel perturbation; the authors also assemble BioleakBench, with 1,600 VQA pairs covering free-form and direct-probe protocols.
AI.result: Across three white-box source models PrivMark achieves up to 85.9% biometric suppression while retaining 75% of clean OK-VQA utility, up to 1.4 times the privacy-utility tradeoff of the strongest pixel-only baseline; the same one-shot perturbations transfer consistently to seven unseen VLMs including closed-source APIs.
AI.conclusion: Protecting privacy at the image level, without access to model internals at deployment, can suppress biometric leakage across VLMs with a favorable privacy-utility trade-off.

title: CompositionEvidence: Controlling Geometric Evidence for Cinematic Composition Reasoning with Frozen Vision-Language Models
comment: Accepted at the 33rd International Conference on MultiMedia Modeling (MMM 2027)
summary: Cinematic composition questions depend on in-frame geometry that vision-language models (VLMs) use inconsistently. External perception tools can expose this geometry, but naive prompt injection can overwrite useful visual predictions. On ShotBench composition, pre-question geometry reduces Qwen2.5-VL-7B from 49.5% to 46.3%; corrupted measurements lower it to 33.6%. CompositionEvidence derives nine reproducible features from frozen detection, depth, and line experts and supplies their shared 24-dimensional representation through two interfaces. A training-free channel appends gated neutral evidence after the question, reaching 56.2% (+6.7, exact McNemar p=0.0018) and 48.4% under corrupted evidence. A minimal-training channel maps the same representation to four soft tokens with a 7.37M-parameter projector while leaving the VLM frozen; it reaches 61.0% (+11.5). Across nine VLMs, including five commercial models queried through official provider APIs, zero-shot accuracy ranges from 43.8% to 63.0%, and the text channel changes it by +6.7 to -6.9 points; the highest baseline is among the regressions. The effect of explicit geometry depends on measurement reliability and on how the receiving model integrates it.

AI.tldr: CompositionEvidence supplies geometric measurements from frozen detection, depth and line experts to frozen VLMs for cinematic composition questions, through a training-free text channel and a minimally trained soft-token channel, with gains that depend on measurement reliability and on how the receiving model integrates the evidence.
AI.motivation: VLMs use in-frame geometry inconsistently, and naive injection of external geometry can overwrite useful visual predictions; on ShotBench composition, pre-question geometry lowers Qwen2.5-VL-7B from 49.5% to 46.3%, and corrupted measurements lower it to 33.6%.
AI.method: Nine reproducible features are derived from the frozen experts and shared as a 24-dimensional representation; a training-free channel appends gated neutral evidence after the question, and a minimal-training channel maps the representation to four soft tokens with a 7.37M-parameter projector while the VLM stays frozen.
AI.result: The text channel reaches 56.2% (+6.7, exact McNemar p=0.0018) and 48.4% under corrupted evidence; the soft-token channel reaches 61.0% (+11.5); across nine VLMs, including five commercial models, zero-shot accuracy ranges from 43.8% to 63.0% and the text channel changes it by +6.7 to -6.9 points, with the highest baseline among the regressions.
AI.conclusion: Explicit geometric evidence helps only when the measurements are reliable and the receiving model integrates them well, so it is not a uniform improvement for VLMs.

title: ZARA: Zero-shot Animatable and Relightable 3D Avatar reconstruction from a single image
summary: Recent large human reconstruction models create remarkable animatable 3D avatars from a single image, but their appearance remains entangled with the illumination and cannot be relighted. In contrast, existing 3D relightable-avatar reconstruction methods typically require person-specific optimization. We present ZARA, a zero-shot feed-forward framework that reconstructs an animatable 3D Gaussian avatar together with its intrinsic attributes from a single image. ZARA couples a pretrained large-scale human reconstruction model with a Material Transformer to inherit geometry priors while learning material-aware Gaussian representations. To preserve localized details, we introduce Gaussian-aligned material feature fusion strategy, which injects multi-scale material features onto individual Gaussians and combines them with geometry tokens. As most human-avatar datasets lack ground-truth material maps, we use pseudo-material labels as conditioning inputs and supervision targets during training. We further introduce MatFace regularization to preserve facial structure and color in albedo prediction under unreliable facial pseudo-material supervision. Extensive experiments demonstrate that ZARA reconstructs animatable and relightable humans within tens of seconds without person-specific optimization or post-processing, outperforming existing baselines in both relighting quality and materials generalization ability. As the ability of recovering the physically-based-rendering attributes of the human, ZARA also enables direct material editing of the avatar's appearance.

AI.tldr: ZARA is a zero-shot feed-forward framework that reconstructs an animatable, relightable 3D Gaussian avatar with intrinsic material attributes from a single image in tens of seconds, without person-specific optimization.
AI.motivation: Large human reconstruction models produce animatable avatars from one image but entangle appearance with illumination so they cannot be relit, while existing relightable avatar methods require per-person optimization.
AI.method: ZARA couples a pretrained large-scale human reconstruction model with a Material Transformer, injects multi-scale material features onto individual Gaussians through Gaussian-aligned material feature fusion, uses pseudo-material labels as conditioning and supervision during training, and adds MatFace regularization to preserve facial structure and color in albedo prediction.
AI.result: Experiments show that ZARA outperforms existing baselines in relighting quality and in generalization of materials, and it supports direct material editing of the avatar; the abstract gives no numeric values.
AI.conclusion: Feed-forward material-aware Gaussian avatars can be recovered from a single image without per-subject optimization or post-processing, enabling relighting and material editing.
