AI.tldr: PTC-IoU is a CPU-based detection quality estimator for edge video analytics that scores detections from compacted box histories. On a Jetson Orin Nano it cuts per-frame estimator latency from 10.3 ms to 2.2 ms, raises pipelined throughput by 13.6% and reduces estimator energy by up to 95%, with competitive detection quality.
AI.motivation: Edge systems lack ground-truth labels at runtime, and detector confidence scores cannot reveal every missed object or misplaced box. Neural quality estimators add GPU workload on top of detection, while CPU capacity often remains idle.
AI.method: Predictive Temporal Consistency IoU (PTC-IoU) moves the estimation workload to the CPU by compacting detection box histories, which supports deterministic result scoring. Its output indicates which frames may contain detection failures and should be escalated to a more powerful cloud model.
AI.result: On Nvidia Jetson Orin Nano, per-frame estimator latency drops from 10.3 ms for neural counterparts to 2.2 ms, a 4.7x speedup. Pipelined throughput increases by 13.6%, and estimator energy consumption is cut by up to 95%. The method maintains competitive final detection quality on multiple datasets.
AI.conclusion: Compacted temporal box-history scoring on the CPU is a practical, cheaper alternative to neural quality estimators for edge video analytics.

title: PhysOPSD: Code as Privilege for Physically Plausible Video Generation
summary: While modern video generative models achieve remarkable visual fidelity, they remain noticeably brittle when generating physically plausible dynamics and complex interactions. Targeted post-training is crucial, yet supervised fine-tuning suffers from offline state mismatch, and reinforcement learning is hindered by sparse, ill-defined physical reward functions. On-Policy (Self-)Distillation (OPSD) reconciles on-policy rollouts with dense corrective feedback, shifting the core challenge to designing effective privileged context. However, conventional modalities fall short: text prompts are inherently declarative, whereas real reference videos heavily entangle physical laws with visual appearance without parametric control. To this end, we propose PhysOPSD, introducing executable code as privileged physical context for video generation. Unlike static visual observations, executable code instantiates an editable physical world with intrinsic abstraction and controllability. Powered by PhysOPSD-Engine, we translate real-world physical scenarios into verifiable simulation programs. PhysOPSD then incorporates (i) dual-level physical privilege to bridge the information gap via an intermediate bottleneck, alongside (ii) controlled physical variations under shared rollout noise to expose causal dynamic shifts. Extensive experiments demonstrate that PhysOPSD substantially improves physical plausibility across diverse backbones, outperforming SFT and RL baselines with only $3$K samples, while preserving general video generation quality.

AI.tldr: PhysOPSD uses executable code as privileged physical context for on-policy self-distillation of video generation models, improving physical plausibility. With only 3K samples it outperforms SFT and RL baselines across diverse backbones while preserving general video quality.
AI.motivation: Video generators remain brittle on physically plausible dynamics. Supervised fine-tuning suffers from offline state mismatch, RL is hindered by sparse and ill-defined physical rewards, and text prompts or real reference videos are poor privileged contexts for physics.
AI.method: The authors propose executable code as privileged physical context. PhysOPSD-Engine translates real-world physical scenarios into verifiable simulation programs. PhysOPSD adds dual-level physical privilege through an intermediate bottleneck and controlled physical variations under shared rollout noise to expose causal dynamic shifts, on top of On-Policy (Self-)Distillation.
AI.result: Extensive experiments show that PhysOPSD substantially improves physical plausibility across diverse backbones. It outperforms SFT and RL baselines using only 3K samples, and it preserves general video generation quality.
AI.conclusion: Executable code is an effective and controllable privileged context for teaching video generators physical dynamics with dense corrective feedback.

title: dNaViT: Discrete Codes are General-Purpose Visual Representations
comment: Technical Report. Project page: this https URL ; Code: this https URL ; Models: this https URL
summary: Discrete autoregressive modeling, notably through next-token prediction, has become a cornerstone of modern language models. Extending this paradigm to vision allows visual and language models to converge on a unified framework, thereby fostering shared methodology and infrastructure. This work investigates a central question: how far can a finite discrete vocabulary go in representing the richness of the visual world? We present dNaViT, a Discrete Native-resolution Vision Transformer that produces discrete visual primitives analogous to language tokens. Built upon a frozen pretrained encoder, dNaViT applies lightweight residual modulation with a dual-branch objective to inject reconstruction-aware cues into semantic features. By leveraging grouped product quantization, it scales discrete capacity without inflating spatial sequence lengths, while a balanced training recipe maintains both semantic and pixel-level information. Consequently, dNaViT functions as a versatile discrete visual tokenizer, enabling unified encoding across downstream tasks alongside high-fidelity image decoding. Extensive evaluations show that dNaViT matches or exceeds task-specific baselines across 12 visual understanding benchmarks, 4 generation benchmarks, and an image editing benchmark. These findings demonstrate that a compact discrete vocabulary can serve as a universal visual currency and unlock the full potential of fully unified, native multimodal methodology.

AI.tldr: dNaViT is a discrete native-resolution vision transformer that produces discrete visual tokens analogous to language tokens, and it works as a unified visual tokenizer for understanding, generation and reconstruction. It matches or exceeds task-specific baselines across 12 understanding benchmarks, 4 generation benchmarks and an image editing benchmark.
AI.motivation: Discrete autoregressive modeling works well for language, and extending it to vision would allow visual and language models to share one framework. The open question is how far a finite discrete vocabulary can represent the richness of visual content.
AI.method: dNaViT builds on a frozen pretrained encoder and adds lightweight residual modulation with a dual-branch objective to inject reconstruction-aware cues into semantic features. Grouped product quantization scales discrete capacity without lengthening spatial sequences, and a balanced training recipe preserves both semantic and pixel-level information.
AI.result: dNaViT matches or exceeds task-specific baselines across 12 visual understanding benchmarks, 4 generation benchmarks and one image editing benchmark. It also supports high-fidelity image decoding.
AI.conclusion: A compact discrete vocabulary can serve as a universal visual currency for unified multimodal modeling.

title: Occupancy Modelling of Biased Landslide Inventories: When Does Separating Occurrence from Recording Improve on Neutralisation?
summary: Landslide susceptibility models are trained on inventories that record where landslides were seen, not where they occurred. The established remedy fits bias-describing variables and neutralises them when mapping. We adapt occupancy-detection modelling from ecology, treating several inventories as imperfect observers of one event and separating occurrence from recording, and ask when this improves on neutralisation. We use near-complete inventories of the 2018 Hokkaido Eastern Iburi, 2015 Gorkha and 2010 Haiti earthquakes with simulated reporting bias, and three real Gorkha inventories. Compared with standard practice, the occupancy model reduces road bias in 24 of 25 paired draws and raises AUC by 0.08-0.14 on Gorkha and 0.03 on Haiti, but only 0.01-0.02 on Iburi. Its median predicted-to-true landslide rate is 0.99 (range 0.44-1.89), against 0.24-0.30 for the baselines. Rescaling the baselines with the same anchor area corrects their median but leaves larger errors (range 0.20-4.34). Cell-level probabilities remain too extreme (calibration slope 0.59). Compared with the best neutralised model, AUC is higher on Iburi (by 0.03-0.07) and lower on Gorkha and Haiti (by 0.01-0.05). Transplant experiments tie the Iburi advantage to the structure of its true landslide pattern, not to its terrain or road network. In all eight settings with a low interaction gap, computable from biased records, neutralisation was at least as accurate, including a prespecified test on Haiti; a high gap did not guarantee an advantage. The real Gorkha inventories are slope-biased, not road-biased, and there the model brings no meaningful gain. Report-based catalogues remain the main untested case.

AI.tldr: The paper adapts occupancy-detection modelling to landslide inventories, treating several inventories as imperfect observers of one event. It finds that separating occurrence from recording helps mainly in some settings, and that neutralisation is at least as accurate in all eight low-interaction-gap settings.
AI.motivation: Landslide susceptibility models are trained on inventories that record where landslides were seen rather than where they occurred. The established remedy fits bias-describing variables and neutralises them at mapping time, and the paper asks when a separate occurrence-recording model improves on this.
AI.method: The authors apply occupancy-detection modelling from ecology to several inventories, separating occurrence from recording. They use near-complete inventories from the 2018 Hokkaido Eastern Iburi, 2015 Gorkha and 2010 Haiti earthquakes with simulated reporting bias, plus three real Gorkha inventories, and compare against standard neutralisation baselines. Transplant experiments are used to probe the source of the Iburi advantage.
AI.result: The occupancy model reduces road bias in 24 of 25 paired draws and raises AUC by 0.08 to 0.14 on Gorkha and by 0.03 on Haiti, but only by 0.01 to 0.02 on Iburi. Its median predicted-to-true landslide rate is 0.99 (range 0.44 to 1.89), against 0.24 to 0.30 for the baselines. Cell-level probabilities remain too extreme (calibration slope 0.59). In all eight settings with a low interaction gap, neutralisation was at least as accurate, and the real Gorkha inventories show no meaningful gain.
AI.conclusion: The occupancy model is not uniformly better than neutralisation. Its advantage depends on the interaction gap and the bias structure, and report-based catalogues remain untested.

title: MoSTE: Mixture of Spatio-Temporal Experts for Deepfake Detection in Videos
comment: Accepted to IEEE/CVF Winter Conference on Applications of Computer Vision (WACV) 2027
summary: Generalizable deepfake video detection remains challenging because forgery artifacts vary substantially across manipulation types and often combine diverse spatial and temporal inconsistencies. Existing parameter-efficient adaptation methods typically rely on a single shared representation, rendering them prone to manipulation-specific bias and limiting transfer to unseen forgeries. To address this challenge, we propose Mixture Of Spatio-Temporal Experts (MoSTE), an adaptation framework that enables conditional specialization of forensic representations. Instead of forcing one adapter to model all forgery patterns, MoSTE decomposes adaptation into parallel spatial and temporal expert pools and dynamically routes tokens to the most relevant experts through an unsupervised token-level routing mechanism. This allows experts to naturally specialize in complementary forgery cues without requiring explicit manipulation labels or multi-stage training, while effectively transferring representations from CLIP to the video domain. Extensive experiments across cross-dataset and cross-manipulation benchmarks demonstrate that MoSTE sets a new state of the art in average generalization while preserving strong performance across diverse manipulation families. Additional analysis of expert routing and attention behavior reveals the emergence of expert diversity, suggesting that MoSTE learns complementary spatio-temporal forensic features. Code is available at this https URL

AI.tldr: MoSTE is a parameter-efficient adaptation framework for deepfake video detection that routes tokens to parallel spatial and temporal expert pools, transferring CLIP to the video domain. It reports a new state of the art in average generalization across cross-dataset and cross-manipulation benchmarks.
AI.motivation: Existing parameter-efficient adapters rely on one shared representation, which causes manipulation-specific bias and limits transfer to unseen forgeries, while forgery artifacts vary widely across manipulation types.
AI.method: MoSTE decomposes adaptation into parallel spatial and temporal expert pools and dynamically routes tokens to the most relevant experts through an unsupervised token-level routing mechanism. Experts specialize without manipulation labels or multi-stage training.
AI.result: MoSTE sets a new state of the art in average generalization on cross-dataset and cross-manipulation benchmarks while keeping strong performance across diverse manipulation families. Analysis of routing and attention shows the emergence of expert diversity.
AI.conclusion: The routed expert design learns complementary spatio-temporal forensic features, improving generalization of deepfake video detection.

title: LongSCOP: Semantically Consistent Long Video Outpainting
summary: Video out-painting is an important problem, yet existing research focuses primarily on short clips, leaving long video out-painting largely underexplored. Extending video out-painting to long videos poses substantial challenges. A natural solution is iterative out-painting, i.e., generating videos chunk by chunk, but this introduces two major issues: generation instability or even failure caused by inter-chunk inconsistencies and error accumulation, and semantic drift over long temporal horizons. In this paper, we propose LongSCOP, short for Semantically Consistent long Video Out-Painting. First, we introduce a training recipe with three components for smooth and stable long-horizon generation: self-forcing training, latent calibration, and future references. Beyond generation stability, we recognize that the rich temporal context of long videos provides valuable references for maintaining semantic consistency. We therefore develop a VLM-based agent that automatically selects the most informative reference frames from the entire video to maintain consistent subjects, scenes, and backgrounds throughout long-horizon generation. We also construct a high-quality training dataset of 62K video clips. To facilitate research on this underexplored problem, we introduce LVO-Bench, a benchmark curated by human experts to assess long-horizon stability and semantic consistency. Extensive experiments demonstrate that our method outperforms existing approaches in both generation stability and semantic coherence.

AI.tldr: LongSCOP is a long-video outpainting method that combines a stable chunk-wise training recipe with a VLM agent that selects informative reference frames to keep subjects, scenes and backgrounds consistent. It is evaluated on a new 62K-clip training dataset and a new benchmark, LVO-Bench.
AI.motivation: Outpainting research focuses on short clips. Iterative chunk-by-chunk outpainting of long videos suffers from inter-chunk inconsistency, error accumulation and semantic drift over long horizons.
AI.method: Three training components provide smooth, stable long-horizon generation: self-forcing training, latent calibration and future references. A VLM-based agent selects the most informative reference frames from the entire video to maintain semantic consistency. The authors build a 62K-clip training dataset and LVO-Bench, a human-curated benchmark for long-horizon stability and semantic consistency.
AI.result: The abstract reports that the method outperforms existing approaches in both generation stability and semantic coherence on extensive experiments. No specific numbers are given in the abstract.
AI.conclusion: Selecting informative reference frames from the whole video, together with stable training, enables semantically consistent long-video outpainting.

title: Perturb, Aggregate then Reconstruct: Consensus Aggregation and Fourier-Attended Multi-Decoders for Reconstruction-based Multi-View Anomaly Detection
comment: 14 pages, 7 figures. Accepted at ACM Multimedia 2026 (MM '26)
summary: Multi-view anomaly detection is crucial for industrial inspection to identify defects hidden from single viewpoints. Yet, despite their strong success in single-view applications, reconstruction-based methods remain largely underexplored in multi-view settings. A key challenge in extending these methods lies in generating view-consistent pseudo-anomalies. To address this, we propose PAR, a reconstruction-based framework for enhanced multi-view anomaly detection. First, we introduce a feature perturbation strategy coupled with a consensus aggregation module that integrates these perturbed features across viewpoints to mitigate view-inconsistent anomalies and construct highly aligned pseudo-anomaly representations. Second, we employ a view-specialized multi-decoder architecture; by assigning a dedicated decoder to each view, we increase the model's representational complexity, enabling the generation of highly feasible, localized anomaly maps rather than less precise, view-agnostic reconstructions. Last, we incorporate Fourier attention into the decoders to emphasize global frequency-domain structures over local token evidence, effectively preventing identity mapping. Extensive experiments on the Real-IAD dataset demonstrate that PAR consistently outperforms state-of-the-art methods in sample-level, image-level, and pixel-level anomaly detection. Our code is available at this https URL.

AI.tldr: PAR is a reconstruction-based multi-view anomaly detection framework that uses consensus-aggregated feature perturbation, view-specialized decoders and Fourier attention to generate view-consistent pseudo-anomalies. It consistently outperforms state-of-the-art methods on Real-IAD at sample, image and pixel levels.
AI.motivation: Reconstruction-based anomaly detection has been studied mainly for single views, and extending it to multi-view inspection is hard because it is difficult to generate view-consistent pseudo-anomalies.
AI.method: A feature perturbation strategy is combined with a consensus aggregation module that merges perturbed features across viewpoints to suppress view-inconsistent anomalies. A dedicated decoder for each view produces localized anomaly maps. Fourier attention in the decoders emphasizes global frequency-domain structure over local token evidence to prevent identity mapping.
AI.result: On the Real-IAD dataset, PAR consistently outperforms state-of-the-art methods in sample-level, image-level and pixel-level anomaly detection.
AI.conclusion: Consensus-aggregated perturbation, per-view decoding and Fourier attention together make reconstruction-based multi-view anomaly detection effective for industrial inspection.

title: MARS: Multiscale Appearance-Residual Streams for Video Forgery Detection
summary: Generalizing deepfake detection across facial manipulation and fully generated video remains challenging due to forgery traces varying with the manipulation method and scene content. Explicit spatial and temporal feature differences offer a way to capture this variation, but also respond to natural texture and motion, motivating their joint interpretation with appearance features. We investigate whether combining multiscale feature differences with adapted appearance representations improves detection across both forgery categories. We introduce Multiscale Appearance-Residual Streams (MARS), a two-path video detector. The residual path applies fixed spatial and temporal difference-of-Gaussians operators to frozen intermediate features and models the resulting differences alongside appearance context across frames. The semantic path adapts the encoder's normalization parameters for frame classification, and a clip-dependent gate combines their predictions. Under a shared protocol across seven datasets, MARS achieves the highest average AUROC of 91.43\%, outperforming seven compared detectors. When trained on facial manipulations alone, MARS achieves 93.99\% AUROC on GenVideo and 75.50\% on DF26, demonstrating transfer to generated videos without generated-video training data. MARS also provides signed patch and frame contributions, whose faithfulness we evaluate through controlled spatial and temporal removal against random controls. MARS is publicly available for research: Project page: this https URL Github: this https URL

AI.tldr: MARS is a two-path video detector that combines multiscale spatial and temporal feature differences with adapted appearance features to detect forged videos, including facial manipulations and fully generated videos. It reaches the highest average AUROC of 91.43% across seven datasets and transfers from facial manipulations to generated videos without generated-video training data.
AI.motivation: Deepfake detection generalizes poorly across facial manipulation and fully generated video because forgery traces vary with the manipulation method and scene content. Explicit feature differences capture this variation but also respond to natural texture and motion, so they need to be interpreted jointly with appearance features.
AI.method: A residual path applies fixed spatial and temporal difference-of-Gaussians operators to frozen intermediate features and models the differences together with appearance context across frames. A semantic path adapts the encoder's normalization parameters for frame classification, and a clip-dependent gate combines the two paths' predictions. The model also provides signed patch and frame contributions.
AI.result: Under a shared protocol on seven datasets, MARS achieves the highest average AUROC of 91.43% and outperforms seven compared detectors. Trained only on facial manipulations, it reaches 93.99% AUROC on GenVideo and 75.50% on DF26. Controlled spatial and temporal removal tests show its contributions are faithful compared with random controls.
AI.conclusion: Joint modelling of multiscale feature differences and appearance features improves cross-category video forgery detection and transfers to generated videos. The signed contribution maps offer interpretability that the paper argues is faithful.

title: EditJudge-Bench: Auditing VLM Image-Edit Judges with Synthetic Ground Truth
comment: Accepted to NeurIPS 2026 (Evaluations & Datasets Track). 26 pages, 6 figures, 5 tables. Project page: this https URL
summary: Vision-language models (VLMs) are increasingly used as automated judges for image-editing benchmarks, yet their reliability is poorly understood. Auditing these judges is difficult because real edited images lack controlled ground truth and entangle the requested changes with model artefacts, unintended side effects, and ambiguous degrees of success. In this paper, we introduce EditJudge-Bench, a diagnostic benchmark of 1,382 synthetic before/after image pairs rendered in Blender, with edits parameterised across nine categories derived from real user requests and exact ground truth from known 3D scene parameters. Because every edit is generated by a known intervention on a controlled scene, EditJudge-Bench evaluates VLM judges as binary verifiers of whether an instruction was correctly executed, isolating judge perception from editor quality. Across 25 judge configurations, we find substantial reliability gaps: (a) the widely adopted VIEScore template reaches only 69.0% AUROC with GPT-4o; (b) fine-tuned judges score 51.7-66.3%; spatial edits such as rotation and shape remain challenging; (c) prompt-formatting choices like image-text ordering shift performance by up to 14.1 points. Despite using only synthetic data, judge rankings on EditJudge-Bench correlate strongly with two real-image human-preference benchmarks ($\rho$=0.95 and $\rho$=0.71), indicating that controlled audits surface failure modes relevant to real evaluation.

AI.tldr: EditJudge-Bench is a diagnostic benchmark of 1,382 synthetic before-and-after image pairs with exact ground truth for auditing vision-language model judges of image edits. It finds substantial reliability gaps across 25 judge configurations, and judge rankings on the synthetic data correlate strongly with two real-image human-preference benchmarks.
AI.motivation: VLMs are increasingly used as automated judges for image-editing benchmarks, but their reliability is poorly understood. Real edited images lack controlled ground truth and entangle the requested change with editor artefacts, side effects and ambiguous success levels, so existing judges cannot be audited cleanly.
AI.method: The benchmark renders 1,382 before-and-after image pairs in Blender, with edits parameterised across nine categories derived from real user requests and ground truth taken from known 3D scene parameters. VLMs are evaluated as binary verifiers of whether an instruction was correctly executed, which isolates judge perception from editor quality.
AI.result: Across 25 judge configurations, the VIEScore template reaches only 69.0% AUROC with GPT-4o, and fine-tuned judges score 51.7% to 66.3%. Spatial edits such as rotation and shape remain hard, and image-text ordering in the prompt shifts performance by up to 14.1 points. Judge rankings correlate with two real-image human-preference benchmarks at rho = 0.95 and rho = 0.71.
AI.conclusion: Controlled synthetic audits expose failure modes of VLM judges that are relevant to real evaluation, so such benchmarks can be used to check judges before they score editing models.

title: WanderBench: Can World Models Explore Dynamic Worlds from Video?
summary: Video world models conditioned on an input video make it possible to explore real, recorded dynamic scenes, enabling re-shooting of footage, free-viewpoint replay, and real-to-sim environments for embodied agents. Such uses require the generated rollout to stay faithful to the recorded world, yet existing benchmarks start from a single image or a text prompt, and video-conditioned generation is evaluated mainly on perceptual quality and camera following. These evaluations do not directly assess whether exploration preserves subject identity, event progression, and scene consistency upon revisiting a location. We introduce WanderBench, a benchmark for exploring dynamic worlds from video. It comprises 745 single-shot source videos of real and AI-generated content in three difficulty tiers (3-25 s), paired with camera routes given as keyboard actions, and evaluates six dimensions with 24 human-validated sub-metrics. Benchmarking eight models, we find that as clips grow longer, models keep the static scene and visual quality but lose camera control and the source dynamics, and that none keeps revisited places consistent. We further propose WanderLand, a training-free framework that conditions each frame of a frozen model on the same-instant source and, on revisits, on its own earlier static content. WanderLand improves five models on every dimension, by up to 8.3 points in source-dynamics fidelity.

AI.tldr: WanderBench is a benchmark for exploring dynamic worlds from a source video, with 745 clips and keyboard camera routes, evaluated on six dimensions with 24 human-validated sub-metrics. The authors also propose WanderLand, a training-free framework that improves five models on every dimension.
AI.motivation: Existing world-model benchmarks start from a single image or text prompt and evaluate video-conditioned generation mainly on perceptual quality and camera following. They do not test whether exploration preserves subject identity, event progression and scene consistency when a location is revisited.
AI.method: WanderBench comprises 745 single-shot source videos of real and AI-generated content in three difficulty tiers of 3 to 25 seconds, paired with keyboard-action camera routes, and scores six dimensions with 24 human-validated sub-metrics. WanderLand conditions each frame of a frozen model on the same-instant source frame and, on revisits, on the model's own earlier static content.
AI.result: Benchmarking eight models shows that as clips grow longer, models keep the static scene and visual quality but lose camera control and source dynamics, and none keeps revisited places consistent. WanderLand improves five models on every dimension, by up to 8.3 points in source-dynamics fidelity.
AI.conclusion: Video world models do not yet explore recorded dynamic scenes faithfully over long horizons, particularly under revisits. The benchmark exposes these failures, and training-free conditioning offers a practical partial remedy.

title: GHiML: VLM-Guided Hierarchical Multi-Label Learning with Applications to Benthic Imagery
summary: Vision language models (VLMs) encode substantial expert knowledge within their weights, yet their direct application to specialised classification domains such as benthic imagery remains limited. Meanwhile, vision transformers trained on these tasks rely predominantly on low-level visual latents (colours, textures, and shapes) that lack the higher-level reasoning humans employ for identification. We propose Guided Hierarchical Multi-Label (GHiML) learning, a pipeline that extracts conceptual latent variables from a VLM conditioned on training data, generates sample-relevant captions grounded in those variables, and fuses the resulting textual embeddings with image embeddings via cross-attention and a per-node gated router. We also introduce the inverted HML score ($d_{\mathrm{inv}}$), a similarity score that evaluates hierarchical multi-label predictions through graph traversal distance and a cardinality penalty, providing an interpretable alternative to existing measures, which are insensitive to realistic degradations in sparse, deep hierarchies. Experiments on BenthicNet, FathomNet and iNaturalist show that the router improves macro $F_1$ over the vision-only baseline by up to 6.7 pp and $d_{\mathrm{inv}}$ by up to 21.1 pp on in-domain benthic data, with gains persisting under distribution shift. Ablations locate the contribution of the text itself: on the multi-label biotic hierarchies, removing the per-sample text signal degrades $d_{\mathrm{inv}}$ while leaving macro $F_1$ unchanged, consistent with text acting through prediction cardinality rather than node discrimination, whereas iNaturalist, whose annotations are single-label, loses 18.7% of macro $F_1$. Our results support the hypothesis that VLMs contain exploitable specialised knowledge that, when appropriately elicited, can augment classification in domains where direct visual learning is insufficient.

AI.tldr: GHiML is a pipeline that extracts conceptual latent variables from a vision-language model and fuses the resulting caption embeddings with image embeddings through cross-attention and a per-node gated router for hierarchical multi-label classification of benthic imagery. It also introduces the inverted HML score, a hierarchical metric based on graph traversal distance and a cardinality penalty.
AI.motivation: VLMs hold expert knowledge but are hard to apply directly to specialised classification domains such as benthic imagery. Vision transformers trained on these tasks rely mainly on low-level visual cues, and existing hierarchical metrics are insensitive to realistic degradations in sparse, deep hierarchies.
AI.method: Conceptual latent variables are extracted from a VLM conditioned on training data, and sample-relevant captions are generated from them. The textual embeddings are fused with image embeddings by cross-attention and a per-node gated router. The inverted HML score d_inv is a similarity measure built on graph traversal distance with a cardinality penalty.
AI.result: On BenthicNet, FathomNet and iNaturalist, the router improves macro F1 over the vision-only baseline by up to 6.7 points and d_inv by up to 21.1 points on in-domain benthic data, with gains persisting under distribution shift. Removing the per-sample text signal lowers d_inv on multi-label hierarchies while leaving macro F1 unchanged, and iNaturalist, which has single-label annotations, loses 18.7% of macro F1.
AI.conclusion: Text elicited from VLMs mainly acts through prediction cardinality rather than node discrimination on multi-label hierarchies. The results support the view that VLMs contain specialised knowledge that can augment classification where direct visual learning is insufficient.

title: Towards Reconstructing and Recognizing Objects behind Fragmented Occlusion using Video
summary: Perceiving objects through fragmented occlusions, such as foliage, is a natural capability of the human visual system but remains a fundamental challenge for computer vision. This work addresses the problem of object reconstruction, or de-occlusion, in the presence of high-density, fragmented occlusions. We propose a reconstruction framework that operates on a sequence of grayscale images of a moving object, acquired by a single camera, either stationary or in motion. The algorithm estimates the object's relative positions across frames by jointly registering the images and optimizing the alignment parameters to maximize the contrast of their average, referred to as the integrated image. This integrated image serves as the reconstructed representation of the object. Experimental evaluations on both synthetic and real video sequences demonstrate the feasibility of accurate reconstruction under occlusion densities exceeding 90%. The proposed approach is competitive with synthetic aperture techniques, which are limited to static objects and require complex camera setup with careful calibration. Furthermore, we show that the integrated image enables reliable object classification under severe occlusion when used as input to standard, off-the-shelf classifiers.

AI.tldr: The paper presents a reconstruction framework that recovers an object hidden behind high-density fragmented occlusion from a grayscale video of a moving object. It estimates inter-frame alignment by maximising the contrast of the averaged image, and the resulting integrated image supports classification under severe occlusion.
AI.motivation: Perceiving objects through fragmented occlusions such as foliage is a basic capability of human vision but remains a hard problem for computer vision. Synthetic aperture techniques can address it, but they are limited to static objects and need complex calibrated camera setups.
AI.method: The algorithm takes a sequence of grayscale frames of a moving object from a single camera, either stationary or in motion. It jointly registers the images and optimises the alignment parameters to maximise the contrast of their average, which is the integrated image used as the reconstruction.
AI.result: Experiments on synthetic and real video show accurate reconstruction at occlusion densities above 90%. The method is competitive with synthetic aperture techniques, and the integrated image supports reliable classification by standard off-the-shelf classifiers under severe occlusion.
AI.conclusion: Video-based joint registration and contrast maximisation offers a feasible, calibration-light route to de-occlusion of moving objects that is competitive with synthetic aperture imaging.

title: When Does Sliced Inference Pay Off? Resolution, Tiling and Dense Fusion for Small Object Detection
summary: Sliced inference such as SAHI is the standard remedy for small objects in high-resolution imagery, but its gains are usually measured against low-resolution baselines. We revisit sliced inference with scale as the explicit variable and ask when tiling actually pays off. We compare seven dense detectors from four families on VisDrone and DOTA, under pre-specified hypotheses, calibration-only tuning and a single evaluation on held-out test data. Two findings emerge. First, much of the benefit attributed to slicing is a resolution effect: on VisDrone, a single pass trained at a higher resolution outperforms tiling with box fusion (merging decoded boxes) for every detector that could be trained at that resolution, and at equal compute a higher resolution helps more than a larger model. Second, tiles carry complementary information that box fusion wastes. We introduce SCAHI (Slicing with Coverage-Aware Hyper Inference), which accumulates the dense outputs of all passes with weights that give every image position the same total coverage, and reads objects off a peak grid fine enough to keep crowded neighbours apart. On identical passes, SCAHI outperforms box fusion for every YOLO detector on both datasets and matches it for FCOS. On DOTA, whose images far exceed the resolution a single pass can be trained at, tiles with SCAHI beat the best single pass for every detector, by 4.3 to 5.6 mAP50 at 2048 px, and replacing only SAHI's merge step by SCAHI adds 2.3 to 4.0 mAP50. An ablation attributes the gain to the border weighting and the resolution of the peak grid. Source code is available at this https URL.

AI.tldr: The paper revisits sliced inference (SAHI) for small object detection with resolution as an explicit variable and shows that much of the gain from slicing is a resolution effect. It introduces SCAHI, which accumulates the dense outputs of all tiles with coverage-aware weights and reads objects from a peak grid, outperforming box fusion for YOLO detectors and matching it for FCOS.
AI.motivation: Sliced inference is the standard remedy for small objects in high-resolution imagery, but its gains have usually been measured against low-resolution baselines. The paper asks when tiling actually pays off once resolution is controlled.
AI.method: Seven dense detectors from four families are compared on VisDrone and DOTA under pre-specified hypotheses, calibration-only tuning and a single evaluation on held-out test data. SCAHI accumulates dense outputs from all passes with weights that give every image position equal total coverage and reads objects off a peak grid fine enough to separate crowded neighbours.
AI.result: On VisDrone, a single pass trained at higher resolution outperforms tiling with box fusion for every detector that can be trained at that resolution. On identical passes, SCAHI beats box fusion for every YOLO detector on both datasets and matches it for FCOS. On DOTA at 2048 px, tiles with SCAHI beat the best single pass by 4.3 to 5.6 mAP50, and replacing only SAHI's merge step adds 2.3 to 4.0 mAP50.
AI.conclusion: Much of the benefit attributed to slicing comes from resolution, but tiles carry complementary information that box fusion discards. Coverage-aware dense accumulation recovers that information, and an ablation attributes the gain to border weighting and the peak grid resolution.

title: What Breaks Scribble-Supervised Segmentation? An Audit-Informed Benchmark for Scribble Annotation Robustness
summary: Scribble-supervised segmentation is typically evaluated with a fixed annotation set, leaving robustness to distinct semantic and geometric imperfections poorly understood. Motivated by an audit of 12,031 manual PASCAL Visual Object Classes (VOC) 2012 scribbles and prior work, we introduce six controlled perturbation operators. Class corruption, spatial offset, and directional perturbation directly operationalize audit signals. Stroke-length reduction is motivated by prior scribble studies, while random dropout and fragmentation serve as diagnostic controls. Each operator reports requested and achieved changes. We evaluate manual and automatic scribbles across two image domains, two principal backbone settings, and multiple training pipelines, with an additional MiT-B1 PFA anchor evaluation. In the five-seed Tree Energy Loss (TEL)-ResNet101 VOC study, mean intersection over union (mIoU) drops from 70.08 to 1.46 under class corruption, compared with 35.57 for spatial offset, 52.20 for directional perturbation, and 63.24 for stroke-length reduction at their strongest settings. At the evaluated endpoints, semantic-anchor corruption produces the largest degradation, while geometric and support responses depend on the pipeline and dataset. Our benchmark provides a reproducible protocol for diagnosing annotation robustness beyond clean-set accuracy. The operator code is available at this https URL.

AI.tldr: The paper introduces an audit-informed benchmark of six controlled perturbation operators for scribble-supervised segmentation, measuring robustness to semantic and geometric annotation errors. Under class corruption, mIoU of the TEL-ResNet101 model on VOC falls from 70.08 to 1.46, the largest degradation of any operator.
AI.motivation: Scribble-supervised segmentation is usually evaluated with a fixed annotation set, so its robustness to semantic and geometric imperfections is poorly understood. The work is motivated by an audit of 12,031 manual PASCAL VOC 2012 scribbles and by prior work.
AI.method: Six perturbation operators are defined: class corruption, spatial offset and directional perturbation directly operationalise the audit signals, stroke-length reduction follows prior scribble studies, and random dropout and fragmentation serve as diagnostic controls. Each operator reports requested and achieved changes, and manual and automatic scribbles are evaluated across two domains, two backbone settings and several training pipelines.
AI.result: In the five-seed TEL-ResNet101 VOC study, mIoU drops from 70.08 to 1.46 under class corruption, compared with 35.57 for spatial offset, 52.20 for directional perturbation and 63.24 for stroke-length reduction at their strongest settings. Semantic-anchor corruption causes the largest degradation, while geometric and support responses depend on the pipeline and dataset.
AI.conclusion: Clean-set accuracy does not reveal annotation robustness, and the proposed protocol offers a reproducible way to diagnose it. Semantic errors in the anchor labels matter most at the evaluated endpoints.

title: National-Scale Crop Type Mapping in Morocco Using Google AlphaEarth Foundations Embeddings and the Fields of the World Field Boundary Map
summary: Recent geospatial foundation models have introduced a new paradigm for large-scale Earth observation by providing pretrained embedding representations that can be directly exploited for downstream tasks. In this work, we investigate the use of Google AlphaEarth Foundations embeddings for national-scale crop type mapping in Morocco. The proposed workflow operates directly on publicly available 64-dimensional pretrained embeddings using lightweight downstream classifiers, eliminating the need to process raw satellite imagery during model training and inference. The approach targets three crop categories, namely winter cereals, tree crops, and other crops. For nationwide inference, the Fields of the World global field boundary map is used to constrain predictions to agricultural parcels, enabling efficient large-scale mapping. Experimental evaluation on an independent test set over ten repeated runs achieved an average classification accuracy of (87.17 +/- 0.42%). Nationwide inference over Morocco was completed in approximately five hours, with the dominant computational cost arising from cloud-based retrieval of the embeddings rather than model execution. These results demonstrate the potential of pretrained embedding representations for computationally efficient national-scale crop type mapping.

AI.tldr: The paper maps crop types across Morocco with lightweight classifiers on 64-dimensional pretrained Google AlphaEarth Foundations embeddings, constrained to agricultural parcels from the Fields of the World boundary map. It reaches 87.17 +/- 0.42% accuracy on an independent test set over ten runs and completes nationwide inference in about five hours.
AI.motivation: Geospatial foundation models provide pretrained embeddings that can be reused for large-scale Earth observation, but their use for national crop mapping has not been tested. Processing raw satellite imagery at national scale is expensive.
AI.method: The workflow uses publicly available 64-dimensional pretrained embeddings and lightweight downstream classifiers, so raw imagery is not processed during training or inference. It targets three crop categories, namely winter cereals, tree crops and other crops, and the Fields of the World field boundary map restricts predictions to agricultural parcels for nationwide inference.
AI.result: On an independent test set over ten repeated runs, the classifier achieves an average accuracy of 87.17 +/- 0.42%. Nationwide inference over Morocco takes about five hours, and most of the cost comes from cloud retrieval of the embeddings rather than model execution.
AI.conclusion: Pretrained embeddings combined with parcel boundaries enable computationally efficient national-scale crop type mapping, and the main cost lies in data retrieval.

title: Differentiable Inverse Rendering Recovers Intrinsic Properties from Intravascular Optical Coherence Tomography
summary: Medical images encode intrinsic tissue properties that indicate disease progression, yet these properties remain entangled with the system-dependent physics of image formation. Differentiable inverse rendering asks whether they are recoverable by inverting the imaging system's forward physics rather than through post-hoc correction. We address this in optical coherence tomography (OCT), focusing on the optical attenuation coefficient, a per-pixel marker of pathology and cellular composition. Conventional recovery relies on closed-form inversions limited to simplified light-tissue models, or learned methods coupled to specific imaging configurations. We instead recover per-pixel attenuation from a single OCT image by gradient descent through a differentiable physics-based forward model. We verified the method against analytical solutions, validated it on five in vitro phantoms, and applied it without modification to 29{,}269 clinical intravascular OCT images from 128 patients. The inversion needs no training data or segmentations and is portable across platforms and retrospective archives. Replacing the forward model or recovering another optical parameter leaves the optimization procedure unchanged. We demonstrate per-pixel recovery is tractable because gradient information scales to this high-dimensional problem, where gradient-free methods become intractable. Our work supports quantitative tissue characterization from OCT images and provides a framework for extension across imaging modalities and organ systems.

AI.tldr: The paper recovers per-pixel optical attenuation coefficients from a single intravascular OCT image by gradient descent through a differentiable physics-based forward model. The method needs no training data or segmentation and is applied without modification to 29,269 clinical images from 128 patients.
AI.motivation: Intrinsic tissue properties indicate disease, but they are entangled with the system-dependent physics of image formation. Existing recovery relies on closed-form inversions that assume simplified light-tissue models or on learned methods tied to specific imaging configurations.
AI.method: The approach inverts the imaging system's forward physics by gradient descent through a differentiable model to recover the attenuation coefficient at every pixel. It is verified against analytical solutions and validated on five in vitro phantoms, and the same optimisation procedure carries over when the forward model is replaced or another optical parameter is recovered.
AI.result: The method agrees with analytical solutions and with five in vitro phantoms, and it is applied without modification to 29,269 clinical intravascular OCT images from 128 patients. The authors attribute tractability at per-pixel scale to gradient information, which remains usable in this high-dimensional problem where gradient-free methods become intractable.
AI.conclusion: Quantitative tissue characterisation from OCT is feasible through differentiable inverse rendering, and the framework can extend to other imaging modalities and organ systems.

title: GeoScope: Training-Free Program Execution beyond the Counting Horizon for Ultra-High-Resolution Remote Sensing Question Answering
comment: Preprint. 72 pages including the Supplementary Material. Project page: this https URL
summary: In ultra-high-resolution (UHR) remote sensing images, the objects that questions count in a region or relate by direction often span only a few pixels. Existing methods mainly decide where a vision-language model (VLM) should look and trust its answer in the chosen view. We show that this assumption fails for counting, and measure VLMs as one calibrates a sensor. All eight open VLMs tested fall increasingly short once a view holds more than a certain number of objects, about five for most on DOTA aerial images. This counting horizon narrows as views grow and objects appear smaller. An empirical power-law response model predicts the undercount a split recovers and the spurious counts it adds, and supports the rule of splitting only views beyond the horizon. In GeoScope, a text-only language model parses the question into a typed spatial program that fixes the region and its resolution. The VLM only grounds and counts within its operating range, and directions are computed explicitly from the grounded boxes. To our knowledge, it is the first UHR method to split views by a measured limit of the VLM. Without training, it improves Qwen3-VL-8B by 16.3 points on regional counting and 10.5 on spatial relations in XLRS-Bench, and has the highest reported accuracy, trained methods included, on regional counting and on the whole benchmark by question. On UHR-Micro it improves global and regional counting by 16.8 and 36.2 points, 15.6 of the former from splitting. On MME-RealWorld counting it gains 11.4 points, and we show that an option that is almost never correct yet often chosen distorts comparisons there. Project page: this https URL

AI.tldr: GeoScope is a training-free method for ultra-high-resolution remote sensing question answering that uses a text-only language model to write a typed spatial program and splits views only beyond a measured counting horizon of the VLM. It improves Qwen3-VL-8B by 16.3 points on regional counting and 10.5 points on spatial relations in XLRS-Bench.
AI.motivation: In ultra-high-resolution remote sensing images, the objects that questions count or relate by direction often span only a few pixels. Existing methods decide where a VLM should look and trust its answer, but this assumption fails for counting because VLMs undercount once a view holds more objects than a limit of about five on DOTA.
AI.method: An empirical power-law response model predicts the undercount that splitting recovers and the spurious counts it adds, and supports splitting only views beyond the counting horizon. A text-only language model parses the question into a typed spatial program that fixes the region and its resolution, the VLM grounds and counts within its operating range, and directions are computed from the grounded boxes.
AI.result: GeoScope improves Qwen3-VL-8B by 16.3 points on regional counting and 10.5 points on spatial relations in XLRS-Bench, with the highest reported accuracy on regional counting and on the whole benchmark by question. On UHR-Micro it improves global and regional counting by 16.8 and 36.2 points, and on MME-RealWorld counting it gains 11.4 points.
AI.conclusion: Splitting views at a measured VLM limit, combined with explicit program execution for spatial reasoning, improves counting and relational questions in ultra-high-resolution imagery without training. The authors also show that a rarely correct but often chosen option can distort benchmark comparisons.

title: OptiCover: A Scalable and Multi-Surface Framework for Cold-Start Visual Optimization under Semantic Constraints
comment: Accepted at GRAIL 2026: Workshop on Generative, Retrieval-augmented, and Agentic Intelligence for Personalization, co-located with CIKM 2026, Rome, Italy
summary: Selecting an effective cover photo is a critical yet understudied problem in visual merchandising for e-commerce marketplaces. On Airbnb, hosts upload many photos depicting different rooms, amenities, and points of interest, but must manually choose a single static cover photo that is reused across heterogeneous product surfaces. This creates substantial challenges: over 90\% of listing photos have no engagement labels, leading to a severe cold-start regime; guest preferences vary across surfaces and search intents, and visually captivating photos may be semantically misaligned with the underlying listing. At Airbnb scale, this corresponds to hundreds of millions of photos and hundreds of thousands of new uploads per day. We propose \emph{OptiCover}, a scalable framework for cold-start visual optimization under semantic constraints and multi-surface engagement signals. The framework combines (i) a photo candidate generator that identifies candidate photos through various proxies, (ii) lightweight vision heads applied to frozen CLIP embeddings for large-scale semantic scoring, (iii) a cross-modal grounding validator based on a vision-language model (VLM) that enforces semantic representativeness, and (iv) an Exploration Logging Module (ELM) that orchestrates the collection of randomized engagement data across heterogeneous product surfaces and contextual search intents. We evaluate OptiCover through extensive offline studies and multiple online experiments across HomePage, and Search surfaces. OptiCover is now deployed in production and performs tens of millions of photo swaps daily. Online results show a 1.5\% engagement lift on the HomePage and a 0.35\% increase in bookers on Search, generating millions of dollars in incremental revenue. Our findings suggest that action-space shaping and semantic constraints are primary drivers of performance.

AI.tldr: OptiCover is a scalable framework for choosing cover photos for Airbnb listings under cold-start conditions and semantic constraints, combining candidate generation, frozen-CLIP heads, a VLM grounding validator and randomized exploration logging. It is deployed in production and gives a 1.5% engagement lift on the HomePage and a 0.35% increase in bookers on Search.
AI.motivation: Hosts must choose one static cover photo that is reused across heterogeneous product surfaces, and over 90% of listing photos have no engagement labels. Guest preferences vary by surface and search intent, and visually appealing photos may not represent the listing.
AI.method: The framework combines a photo candidate generator based on proxies, lightweight vision heads on frozen CLIP embeddings for semantic scoring, a VLM-based cross-modal grounding validator that enforces semantic representativeness, and an Exploration Logging Module that collects randomized engagement data across surfaces and search intents.
AI.result: Offline studies and multiple online experiments on HomePage and Search show a 1.5% engagement lift on the HomePage and a 0.35% increase in bookers on Search. The system is deployed and performs tens of millions of photo swaps daily, generating millions of dollars in incremental revenue.
AI.conclusion: Action-space shaping and semantic constraints are the main drivers of performance in cold-start cover photo optimisation at marketplace scale.

title: Plant Orbiter: 3D Plant Reconstruction and Generation with Video Diffusion Orbit Cameras and 3D Gaussian Splatting
comment: Submitted to Plant Phenomics. 16 pages, 6 figures, 5 tables
summary: Modern digital phenotyping pipelines require the precise measurement of a range of 3D morphological plant traits. The accurate, high throughput acquisition of these traits helps breeders and researchers accelerate the development of new varieties, techniques and products. Recent advances in 3D technologies have enabled a rapid transition from 2D to 3D pipelines, but high throughput acquisition of digital 3D twins of plants remains a significant challenge due to complex morphology, thin structures and occlusions. In this paper we present Plant Orbiter, a new approach to generating 3D plants that leverages recent advances in video diffusion to produce high quality 3D Gaussian Splats of plants from a single image. We show that our method more accurately recreates plant morphology than other state-of-the-art methods, achieving the highest 3D F-score against all baselines, while being more practical for high throughput pipelines due to easier alignment and reduced cost of camera placement. Combined with a 2D diffusion model, we show that our method also achieves state-of-the-art results in the generation of 3D plant models from a text prompt.

AI.tldr: Plant Orbiter generates 3D plant models as 3D Gaussian Splats from a single image by using video diffusion to produce orbit camera views. It achieves the highest 3D F-score against all baselines and also generates 3D plant models from a text prompt when combined with a 2D diffusion model.
AI.motivation: High-throughput acquisition of digital 3D plant twins for phenotyping is hard because of complex morphology, thin structures and occlusions. Existing 3D pipelines require demanding camera placement and alignment.
AI.method: The approach uses recent video diffusion to generate orbit camera views of a plant from one image and reconstructs them as 3D Gaussian Splats. A 2D diffusion model is combined with it for text-prompt generation.
AI.result: The method recreates plant morphology more accurately than other state-of-the-art methods and achieves the highest 3D F-score against all baselines. It also achieves state-of-the-art results for generating 3D plant models from text prompts.
AI.conclusion: Video diffusion orbit views offer a more practical route to 3D plant reconstruction, with easier alignment and lower camera-placement cost, for high-throughput phenotyping pipelines.

title: Complementarity-Driven Dual-Teacher Hierarchical Alignment for Zero-Shot EEG-to-Image Retrieval
summary: Decoding visual information from EEG is central to brain--computer interfaces and brain-inspired intelligence, and contrastive alignment with pretrained vision foundation models (VFMs) has become the dominant paradigm. However, existing methods align EEG solely with CLIP-family VFMs, leaving hierarchical visual information in neural responses under-exploited. To address this gap, we formulate a mechanism-paradigm correspondence view linking hierarchical visual processing (from appearance to semantics) to the complementary biases of cross-paradigm VFMs, with image-only models (e.g., DINO) and image--text models (e.g., CLIP) capturing distinct facets of this hierarchy. Guided by this view, we propose the Dual-Teacher Hierarchical Alignment (DTHA) framework. Concretely, a shared EEG encoder is supervised by frozen multi-blur CLIP and shallow DINOv2 teachers via dual-branch contrastive alignment, so each branch fully supervises the visual cues it emphasizes. A fused-retrieval objective learns adaptive weights to combine their complementary visual representations for zero-shot EEG-to-image retrieval. For the shared EEG encoder, we introduce the Attentive Modulated Scalp-Pattern Bank Encoder (AMSPBE), combining temporo-spatial attention with a learnable scalp-pattern bank for accurate, interpretable visual feature extraction, while modeling regional temporal dynamics and filter-bank topographies. On THINGS-EEG zero-shot retrieval, DTHA achieves 92.4% Top-1 accuracy, exceeding prior state of the art by 12.4 percentage points. Spatial, spectral, and representational-similarity analyses, together with THINGS-MEG evaluation, validate DTHA's effectiveness, biological plausibility, and cross-modality generalization. This complementarity-driven perspective shows that supervision from cross-paradigm VFMs enables more complete extraction of hierarchical visual information from brain activity.

AI.tldr: DTHA aligns EEG signals with two complementary frozen vision teachers, a multi-blur CLIP and a shallow DINOv2, for zero-shot EEG-to-image retrieval. It reaches 92.4% Top-1 accuracy on THINGS-EEG, exceeding the prior state of the art by 12.4 percentage points.
AI.motivation: Existing EEG alignment methods use only CLIP-family vision foundation models, which leaves the hierarchical visual information in neural responses under-exploited. Image-only models such as DINO and image-text models such as CLIP are argued to capture different facets of the appearance-to-semantics hierarchy.
AI.method: A shared EEG encoder is supervised by frozen multi-blur CLIP and shallow DINOv2 teachers through dual-branch contrastive alignment. An adaptive fused-retrieval objective learns weights that combine the complementary representations. The Attentive Modulated Scalp-Pattern Bank Encoder combines temporo-spatial attention with a learnable scalp-pattern bank and models regional temporal dynamics and filter-bank topographies.
AI.result: On THINGS-EEG zero-shot retrieval, DTHA achieves 92.4% Top-1 accuracy, 12.4 points above the prior state of the art. Spatial, spectral and representational-similarity analyses, together with THINGS-MEG evaluation, are reported to support its effectiveness, biological plausibility and cross-modality generalization.
AI.conclusion: Supervision from cross-paradigm vision foundation models extracts hierarchical visual information from brain activity more completely than single-paradigm supervision.

title: 2D Gum-Net: Unsupervised Dense Elastic Image Registration via Symmetric Correlation and Spectral Pooling
comment: 19 pages, 11 figures, 3 tables. Accepted at the NewInML Workshop at the 40th Conference on Neural Information Processing Systems (NeurIPS 2026)
summary: Dense non-rigid registration, the recovery of a pixel-wise deformation field that warps one image into geometric agreement with another, is fundamental across medical imaging, structural biology, and correspondence estimation, yet learning-based approaches face a severe bottleneck: ground-truth deformation fields are notoriously difficult to obtain for real data. We present 2D Gum-Net, an end-to-end architecture that predicts dense elastic deformation fields fully unsupervised. We transfer the Geometric Unsupervised Matching Network (Gum-Net), originally developed for 3D subtomogram alignment in cryo-electron tomography, to 2D elastic registration: all three modules are redesigned in 2D, and the rigid transformation head is replaced by a Dense Spatial Transformer that regresses a sparse control-point grid, lifted to a full-resolution field $\Phi$ by bicubic interpolation. Downsampling uses DCT spectral pooling, implemented as frozen-basis matrix multiplications ($\approx 50\times$ GPU speedup), preserving the fine, quasi-periodic structure that max and average pooling destroy. We evaluate on contact-based fingerprints, a challenging testbed for this task: locally self-similar ridge patterns make correspondence maximally ambiguous, skin pressed against a sensor generates authentic large-displacement elastic distortion, and minutiae act as precise landmarks through which an independent matcher externally verifies the topological correctness of predicted fields. Trained purely on synthetic impressions and evaluated zero-shot on real benchmarks, our method improves structural correlation by up to 15.7% on FVC2004 and raises genuine match scores under an independent matcher while leaving imposter scores essentially unchanged. This suggests that the predicted deformations restore true structure without fabricating correspondences.

AI.tldr: 2D Gum-Net is an unsupervised architecture for dense elastic image registration that predicts pixel-wise deformation fields, adapted from a 3D subtomogram alignment network. It uses DCT spectral pooling and a dense spatial transformer, and trained only on synthetic fingerprints it improves structural correlation by up to 15.7% on FVC2004.
AI.motivation: Learning-based dense non-rigid registration is bottlenecked by the scarcity of ground-truth deformation fields for real data. Max and average pooling destroy the fine, quasi-periodic structure that matters for elastic registration of ridge patterns.
AI.method: The network transfers Gum-Net to 2D with all three modules redesigned, and replaces the rigid head with a Dense Spatial Transformer that regresses a sparse control-point grid lifted to a full-resolution field by bicubic interpolation. Downsampling uses DCT spectral pooling implemented as frozen-basis matrix multiplications, which gives about a 50 times GPU speedup.
AI.result: Trained purely on synthetic impressions and evaluated zero-shot on real benchmarks, the method improves structural correlation by up to 15.7% on FVC2004. It raises genuine match scores under an independent matcher while leaving imposter scores essentially unchanged.
AI.conclusion: The predicted deformations restore true structure without fabricating correspondences, which suggests the approach is useful for unsupervised elastic registration of contact-based fingerprints.

title: What kills $v$-prediction? A Patch-wise PCA Perspective on Pixel-Space Flow Matching
comment: Accepted as a Spotlight paper at NeurIPS 2026. Our code is available at this https URL
summary: Latent Diffusion Models dominate generative modeling but face two-stage training complexity and the inherent reconstruction limits of pre-trained autoencoders. Pixel-space Flow Matching offers a simplified end-to-end alternative yet often encounters training difficulties when using the standard $v$-prediction objective. Recent research attributes this difficulty to the off-manifold nature of noised targets, motivating a shift toward $x$-prediction. In this paper, we investigate this explanation through patch-wise Principal Component Analysis (PCA) and identify a bandwidth bottleneck. The velocity in minor components is largely determined by the raw noisy input, requiring deep backbones to preserve information that competes with principal-component modeling. Through controlled experiments and representation analysis, we further examine why $x$-prediction remains effective: its parameterization provides a raw-input bypass, while its learned input representation can spontaneously concentrate on principal directions. Under low-rank observations, our analysis of the induced flow characterizes $x$-prediction as an implicit conditional-mean decoder, reconstructing discarded components from the retained information. These observations motivate the Raw-injected Transformer (RiT), which combines a lightweight raw-conditioned decoder with an output-side shortcut to separate semantic modeling from raw-state propagation. Our method restores effective $v$-prediction and achieves competitive performance on ImageNet $256\times256$, providing a perspective on the interaction between prediction objectives and architectural bandwidth.

AI.tldr: The paper explains why v-prediction struggles in pixel-space flow matching through a patch-wise PCA analysis, and proposes the Raw-injected Transformer (RiT) to restore effective v-prediction. RiT achieves competitive performance on ImageNet 256x256.
AI.motivation: Pixel-space flow matching avoids the two-stage training and reconstruction limits of latent diffusion but often fails with the standard v-prediction objective. Recent work attributes this to the off-manifold nature of noised targets and moves to x-prediction, and the reason x-prediction works has not been explained.
AI.method: Patch-wise PCA identifies a bandwidth bottleneck, because velocity in minor components is largely determined by the raw noisy input and requires deep backbones to preserve it. Controlled experiments and representation analysis show that x-prediction has a raw-input bypass and learns input representations that concentrate on principal directions. RiT adds a lightweight raw-conditioned decoder and an output-side shortcut that separate semantic modelling from raw-state propagation.
AI.result: The method restores effective v-prediction and achieves competitive performance on ImageNet 256x256. Under low-rank observations, the analysis characterises x-prediction as an implicit conditional-mean decoder that reconstructs discarded components from retained information.
AI.conclusion: Interaction between prediction objective and architectural bandwidth determines whether v-prediction works in pixel space, and separating raw-state propagation from semantic modelling is a workable design.

title: AI-based characterization of lymphoid structures and the tumor microenvironment reveals lower mature tertiary lymphoid structures, lymph-node follicles, and plasma cells after neoadjuvant therapy in lung squamous cell carcinoma
summary: Mature, germinal centre-bearing tertiary lymphoid structures (TLS) and mature lymph node follicles (secondary lymphoid structures, SLS) sustain the plasma cell response that shapes outcome and immunotherapy benefit in lung cancer. How this loco-regional axis differs between neoadjuvant-treated and therapy-naive tumors is poorly defined. We analyzed H&E whole-slide images of resected tumors and paired proximal and distal lymph nodes from matched neoadjuvant-treated (neoLUSC, n=20) and therapy-naive (naivLUSC, n=20) lung squamous cell carcinoma (LUSC) patients. Aignostics Atlas H&E Tissue Analysis (HETA) models quantified cell densities per tissue compartment and cell-cell co-localization; a dedicated deep-learning model validated against pathologist annotations detected TLS and SLS and graded their maturity. Prognostic value was tested in an independent cohort (n=458; 46 treated). In neoLUSC tumors, stromal plasma cell density was 72% (p=0.004) and stromal lymphocyte density 48% (p=0.015) lower than in naivLUSC; macrophages and granulocytes did not differ significantly. Total and immature TLS did not differ, whereas mature TLS in the tumor (p=0.034) and mature SLS in the tumor-distal lymph node (p=0.003) were lower in neoLUSC patients. Peri-TLS plasma cell density correlated with tumor lymphocyte density in naivLUSC (rho=0.54, p=0.017) but not in neoLUSC tumors (rho=0.07). In the validation cohort, stromal plasma cell density (HR 0.69, p=0.011) and lymphocyte-plasma cell co-localization (HR 0.66, p=0.004) were associated with longer survival, and neoadjuvant status with shorter survival (HR 1.50, p=0.026). Neoadjuvant therapy is thus associated with fewer mature lymphoid structures and weaker coupling of the humoral compartment to the tumor rather than uniformly lower immune readouts. The stromal plasma cell/co-localization axis is a candidate prognostic biomarker.

AI.tldr: Using AI-based H&E analysis of matched neoadjuvant-treated and therapy-naive lung squamous cell carcinoma, the study finds fewer mature tertiary lymphoid structures, mature lymph node follicles and stromal plasma cells after neoadjuvant therapy. Stromal plasma cell density and lymphocyte-plasma cell co-localization are associated with longer survival in an independent cohort of 458 patients.
AI.motivation: Mature tertiary lymphoid structures and lymph node follicles sustain the plasma cell response that shapes outcome and immunotherapy benefit in lung cancer. How this loco-regional axis differs between neoadjuvant-treated and therapy-naive tumours is poorly defined.
AI.method: H&E whole-slide images of resected tumours and paired proximal and distal lymph nodes from 20 neoadjuvant-treated (neoLUSC) and 20 therapy-naive (naivLUSC) patients were analysed with the Aignostics Atlas H&E Tissue Analysis models for cell densities and co-localization. A deep-learning model validated against pathologist annotations detected and graded TLS and SLS maturity. Prognostic value was tested in an independent cohort of 458 patients, 46 of them treated.
AI.result: In neoLUSC tumours, stromal plasma cell density was 72% lower (p=0.004) and stromal lymphocyte density 48% lower (p=0.015) than in naivLUSC. Mature TLS in the tumour (p=0.034) and mature SLS in the tumour-distal lymph node (p=0.003) were lower, while total and immature TLS did not differ. In the validation cohort, stromal plasma cell density (HR 0.69) and lymphocyte-plasma cell co-localization (HR 0.66) were associated with longer survival, and neoadjuvant status with shorter survival (HR 1.50).
AI.conclusion: Neoadjuvant therapy is associated with fewer mature lymphoid structures and weaker coupling of the humoral compartment to the tumour, rather than uniformly lower immune readouts. The stromal plasma cell and co-localization axis is a candidate prognostic biomarker.

title: SWAM: Scaling World Action Models with Cross-Modal Alignment
summary: World action models jointly predict video and actions conditioned on language. Existing studies focus primarily on architectures and training mechanisms, typically treating language-video alignment acquired through video pretraining as an established foundation. However, introducing action learning may impair this alignment. Principled guidance on data and supervision design for maintaining language-video alignment during action learning remains limited. To investigate this, we curate a pool of approximately 47,000 hours of general videos, egocentric videos, UMI demonstrations, and robot demonstrations. Building on this, we systematically study how language-video supervision, language-video-action supervision, and the joint use of these two forms affect WAM performance. In particular, we examine how language annotation quality affects pretrained language-video capabilities, and how action supervision from UMI and robot demonstrations extends these capabilities to language-video-action modeling. To better scale the model, we further conduct detailed studies on joint training recipe and model architecture. Under a fixed training budget, mixing egocentric videos and UMI demonstrations improves control generalization. Model architecture affects how effectively these experiences are used, while scaling pretraining under the selected configuration brings further gains. The resulting recipe, post-trained on RoboTwin Clean demonstrations only, achieves success rates of 88.10% and 61.56% under Easy (Clean-to-Clean) and Hard (Clean-to-Random) conditions, respectively. Our model achieves 40.00% SR across three real-world tasks, compared with 23.33% for the strongest baseline, indicating better generalization under unseen conditions. We release the curated data, training code, and model weights.

AI.tldr: SWAM studies how to preserve language-video alignment while training world action models that predict video and actions from language, using about 47,000 hours of mixed video and demonstration data. The resulting recipe reaches 88.10% and 61.56% success on RoboTwin Easy and Hard conditions and 40.00% across three real-world tasks.
AI.motivation: World action models may lose the language-video alignment acquired in video pretraining when action learning is added, and principled guidance on data and supervision for preserving it is limited.
AI.method: About 47,000 hours of general videos, egocentric videos, UMI demonstrations and robot demonstrations are curated. The authors systematically compare language-video supervision, language-video-action supervision and their joint use, study annotation quality and training recipe and architecture, and vary the scale of pretraining under a fixed training budget.
AI.result: Under a fixed budget, mixing egocentric videos and UMI demonstrations improves control generalization. The recipe, post-trained on RoboTwin Clean demonstrations only, achieves 88.10% success under Easy (Clean-to-Clean) and 61.56% under Hard (Clean-to-Random) conditions. It reaches 40.00% success across three real-world tasks, against 23.33% for the strongest baseline.
AI.conclusion: Data mixture, supervision design and architecture choices together determine how well language-video alignment survives action learning, and scaling pretraining adds further gains. The curated data, training code and model weights are released.

title: Click3R: Interactive Stereo 3D Reconstruction with Sparse Correspondence Clicks
comment: NeurIPS 2026. Project page: this https URL
summary: Despite impressive progress, existing feed-forward large 3D reconstruction models produce a single, irrevocable prediction. When these models fail, there is no mechanism to correct their mistakes. To address this limitation, we introduce Click3R, a framework for interactive geometric correction of feed-forward models using sparse human correspondence clicks. Given an image pair and a small set of cross-view point correspondences provided by a user, Click3R injects geometric constraints into the 3D reconstruction networks through a lightweight point correspondence adapter, enabling the model to resolve ambiguities in challenging scenarios such as repetitive textures, symmetric structures, large viewpoint changes, or textureless regions. To evaluate interactive reconstruction, we curate a challenging benchmark specifically designed to expose failure modes of existing feed-forward 3D reconstruction methods. Experiments show that Click3R reduces reconstruction error with as few as a single correspondence click, improving performance on both standard and our curated benchmarks. Our results highlight that sparse human interaction provides an effective and practical mechanism for correcting geometric reconstruction errors.

AI.tldr: Click3R lets a user correct feed-forward stereo 3D reconstruction models with sparse cross-view correspondence clicks, injected through a lightweight point correspondence adapter. A single click reduces reconstruction error, and the authors release a benchmark of challenging failure cases.
AI.motivation: Feed-forward large 3D reconstruction models produce a single irrevocable prediction and offer no way to correct their failures. Ambiguities such as repetitive textures, symmetric structures, large viewpoint changes and textureless regions are hard for them to resolve.
AI.method: Given an image pair and a small set of user-provided cross-view point correspondences, Click3R injects these geometric constraints into the 3D reconstruction networks through a lightweight point correspondence adapter. A new benchmark is curated to expose failure modes of existing feed-forward reconstruction methods.
AI.result: Click3R reduces reconstruction error with as few as a single correspondence click and improves performance on both standard and the curated benchmark.
AI.conclusion: Sparse human interaction is an effective and practical mechanism for correcting geometric reconstruction errors in feed-forward 3D models.

title: Grasping the Future: Joint 3D Hand-Object Forecasting From Internet Videos
summary: To interact with an object, we need to anticipate both how it will move and how our hands should move with it. Human videos capture these relationships across everyday activities, offering a natural source for learning to predict future interactions.
